item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA HOSTS PRESIDENT OF THE SWISS CONFEDERATION
CLOSE COOPERATION BETWEEN INDIA AND SWITZERLAND CAN BRING IMMENSE BENEFITS TO OUR PEOPLE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 10:40PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu received H.E. Mr Guy Parmelin, President of the Swiss Confederation at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (October 5, 2026). She also hosted a banquet in his honour.

Welcoming President Parmelin to India, the President said that India and Switzerland enjoy warm and cordial relations based on the shared values of democracy and the rule of law. We have extensive cooperation across a wide range of areas, including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation, culture, and people-to-people contacts. Regular high-level exchanges between our two countries have continued to provide momentum to our bilateral relations.

The President said that Switzerland is an important trade and investment partner for India. She noted that following the implementation of the historic India-European Free Trade Association Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement, there are even greater opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and investment.

The President noted that Swiss companies have invested in India in important sectors and they have a notable presence in India’s infrastructure sector, particularly in the construction of roads, railway bridges and tunnels. She said that they can also explore opportunities in emerging areas such as clean and green technology and Artificial Intelligence.

The President was happy to note that important agreements have been signed during the visit to promote cooperation in migration and mobility, research, and technology transfer.

The two leaders agreed that close cooperation between India and Switzerland can bring immense benefits to the people of both countries. They expressed confidence that this visit will contribute to further strengthening relations between the two countries.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India and Japan Launch Operational Manual for the Joint Crediting Mechanism
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 8:26PM by PIB Delhi

On 30th September, 2026, Ambassador of Japan to India, H.E. Mr. Keiichi Ono and the then Secretary (MoEFCC), Shri Tanmay Kumar, jointly launched the Operational Manual for the India–Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM), in New Delhi.

The Joint Crediting Mechanism between India and Japan aims to promote the deployment of advanced low-carbon technologies, mobilize climate finance, facilitate technology cooperation and support high-integrity emission reductions and removals in India. The mechanism will contribute to sustainable development in India while strengthening confidence and transparency in international carbon markets.

The launch of the Manual marks a significant milestone in operationalizing bilateral cooperation between India and Japan under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement, following the signing of Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) on 7th August 2025 and adoption of the Rule of Implementation (RoI) on 8th June 2026.

The development signals a transition from institutional preparation to implementation and establishes a clear, transparent and comprehensive procedural framework for implementing activities under India-Japan JCM. The manual provides detailed procedures covering the entire project cycle—from the submission of a Project Idea Note to the issuance and authorization of JCM credits.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Textiles
Ministry of Textiles Organises Swachhta and Cleanliness Activities on Gandhi Jayanti under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 8:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Textiles observed Gandhi Jayanti on 2 October 2026 with a series of Swachhta and cleanliness activities under Special Campaign 6.0, reaffirming its commitment to promoting cleanliness, hygiene and a culture of responsible workplace practices.

The programme was led by Secretary (Textiles) at the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), Delhi, and was attended by senior officers of the Ministry of Textiles, faculty members and staff of NIFT Delhi. On the occasion, the Swachhta Pledge was administered, with participants reaffirming their commitment to maintaining cleanliness and contributing towards a cleaner and healthier environment.

A cleanliness drive was also undertaken at the NIFT Delhi campus, with active participation of officers, faculty and staff. The activities focused on improving cleanliness and upkeep of the premises, promoting proper waste management and sensitising participants towards maintaining clean and hygienic surroundings.

The observance of Gandhi Jayanti under Special Campaign 6 underscores the Ministry of Textiles’ continued efforts to institutionalise Swachhta in its offices and field establishments and to encourage collective participation in creating clean, well-maintained and sustainable workplaces. The Ministry continues to accord priority to cleanliness, disposal of obsolete and unusable items, better workplace management and sustained improvement in cleanliness standards as part of the Special Campaign.

Textile Waste Collection Drive starting this Gandhi Jayanti

As part of the initiative, starting this Gandhi Jayanti, 2nd October 2026, a dedicated textile waste collection bins have been installed at various locations. The initiative seeks to further strengthen the spirit of Jan Bhagidari and collective action towards a clean and sustainable India, with emphasis on cleanliness, responsible waste management, and the adoption of sustainable practices.

The initiative aims to promote responsible collection, segregation, recycling and upcycling of post-consumer textile waste and to encourage sustainable waste-management practices in Central Government office complexes and residential colonies in New Delhi. All officers and officials have been requested to actively participate in the drive by bringing and depositing their post-consumer textile waste in the designated collection bins during the campaign period

As part of the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6, Officers and employees of the attached and subordinate offices of Ministry of Textiles actively participated in the Swachhta Pledge, reaffirming their commitment towards cleanliness, hygiene and maintaining a clean and sustainable working environment.

          

As part of the campaign, a comprehensive cleanliness and de-cluttering drive was undertaken at the National Jute Board premises at Patsan Bhawan, Kolkata, and the Regional Office, New Delhi, from 2nd to 4th October 2026                     

Before                                                                                             After

The Ministry of Textiles continues to make concerted efforts towards achieving the objectives of Special Campaign 6, with a particular focus on Swachhta, cleanliness, space management, disposal of pending references and e-waste management.

item.title: CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana
item.category: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

item.description: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has further intensified its coordinated field-level monitoring mechanism for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana. As part of the monitoring mechanism, Flying Squads have been deployed in 34 districts across the two States…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has further intensified its coordinated field-level monitoring mechanism for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana. As part of the monitoring mechanism, Flying Squads have been deployed in 34 districts across the two States for the period from 01.10.2026 to 30.11.2026, following a communication made by CAQM to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).

 

CAQM intensifies field-level monitoring with deployment of Flying Squads to prevent paddy stubble burning incidents in Punjab and Haryana. For more details, visit: https://t.co/u3EqSC98CP https://t.co/AIZp3UdZJL

— Commission for Air Quality Management (@CAQM_Official) October 5, 2026

 

Accordingly, Flying Squads have been deployed across the identified districts of Punjab and Haryana. The deployment covers 18 districts in Punjab and 16 districts in Haryana, providing extensive field-level monitoring across the two States during the critical paddy harvesting period.

The Flying Squads will assess the ground-level situation in their respective allocated districts and coordinate closely with the concerned authorities and field-level stakeholders for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning. The teams will coordinate with farmers, Parali Protection Force, district-level authorities, State Government Nodal Officers, officers of the respective State Pollution Control Boards, CAQM Cell at SAS Nagar and the Commission. The ground situation, along with the steps taken to prevent further incidents of paddy stubble burning, will be reported to the CAQM Cell on a daily basis.

The deployment has been structured in successive phases, with Flying Squads assigned to respective districts for different deployment periods to ensure sustained field-level monitoring throughout the paddy harvesting season 2026. The district-wise deployment covers key paddy-producing districts in Punjab, including Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Firozpur, Muktsar, Bathinda, Amritsar, Moga, Mansa, Fazilka, Patiala, Ludhiana, Kapurthala, Faridkot, Barnala, Malerkotla, Gurdaspur, Jalandhar and Fatehgarh Sahib. In Haryana, the deployment covers Jind, Fatehabad, Hisar, Kaithal, Sonipat, Rohtak, Sirsa, Karnal, Palwal, Jhajjar, Kurukshetra, Ambala, Yamunanagar, Faridabad, Panipat and Hansi.

The strengthened field-level mechanism is aimed at ensuring timely assessment of the on-ground situation, close coordination among enforcement agencies and prompt preventive action to tackle stubble burning incidents during the harvesting season. The daily field-level reports from the Flying Squads will also facilitate continuous assessment of the situation by the Commission and enable coordinated follow-up with the concerned authorities, wherever required.

CAQM has been continuously monitoring, coordinating and reviewing the implementation of measures for prevention of paddy stubble burning with the concerned State Governments, State Pollution Control Boards and District Administrations. The Commission has reiterated the need for concerted efforts by all concerned agencies, along with active facilitation and cooperation of farmers and other stakeholders, to ensure prevention of stubble burning during the season.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
IICA observed 3rd IICA CSR Day on Gandhi Jayanti with a Special Address by the DG & CEO to Participants of the IICA Certified CSR Professional Programme ahead of NCCSR 2026
NCCSR 2026, on 6th–7th October in New Delhi, to provide a national platform for dialogue, collaboration and knowledge-sharing on CSR
CSR in India has its foundation in Indian tradition and in the concept of trusteeship, and did not emerge only from the Companies Act: Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, DG  & CEO, IICA
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 7:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), under the aegis of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, observed CSR Day recently on the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General & CEO, IICA, delivered a Special Address to the Participants of Batch 11 of the IICA Certified CSR Professional Programme. The session, organised virtually by the School of Business Environment, IICA, also served as the curtain-raiser to the 3rd National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026).

The observance draws on a suggestion made by the then Hon'ble President of India, Shri Ram Nath Kovind, at the National CSR Awards in 2019, that 2nd October be dedicated to Corporate Social Responsibility. Rooted in Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy of trusteeship, IICA CSR Day provides a platform for dialogue, recognition, collaboration and knowledge-sharing on India's evolving CSR ecosystem.

Welcoming the DG & CEO, Dr. Garima Dadhich, Head, School of Business Environment and Course Director, said that what the CSR ecosystem needs in greater numbers is trained professionals with the capacity to turn an obligation into an outcome. She emphasised that the programme has been linked with the National Conference as part of its curriculum for this purpose, and informed that NCCSR 2026 has drawn over 550 delegates from across India.

In his address, Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh said that 2nd October and CSR are philosophically connected, as CSR in India has its foundation in Indian tradition and in the concept of trusteeship, and did not emerge only from the Companies Act. Referring to Section 166(2) of the Companies Act, 2013, he said the law itself recognises that a company operates within society and owes responsibility to its employees, the community and the environment, and not to shareholders alone.

Tracing the evolution of the framework, he said that CSR expenditure has grown from about ₹10,000 crore in the first year of the mandate to nearly ₹35,000 crore in FY 2023–24. He described the journey from the early "comply or explain" phase to the 2019 amendments and the 2021 Rules, which introduced the Unspent CSR Account, multi-year projects, certification of fund utilisation and impact assessment. He said that CSR should not be seen as deficit financing that merely supplements government spending. Its purpose is to leverage corporate resources, technology and expertise to create a multiplier effect and to test innovative approaches in the social sector.

He observed that a significant part of CSR remains supply-driven, with projects chosen on the basis of familiar areas, geographies and agencies, and called for needs-based CSR with community participation, a standard operating procedure for need assessment and social impact assessment, and stronger capacity among implementing agencies. He highlighted the CSR Exchange Portal of the Ministry as a platform on which district administrations, organisations and communities can place documented needs before companies, and also encouraged companies in the same sector to pool resources for high-impact national projects.

On Viksit Bharat, he said the goal should not be seen only in terms of the size of the economy and that "Viksit Bharat also requires developed thinking and a developed social consciousness," he said. He further concluded by calling for a shift from spending to transforming, from compliance to commitment, from reporting to evidence, and from isolated initiatives to collaboration, supported by technology-enabled monitoring, and urged the Participants to become ambassadors of this CSR philosophy.

NCCSR 2026 will be held on 6th–7th October 2026 at The Ashok, New Delhi, on the theme ‘Re-envisioning the Spirit of CSR for Viksit Bharat: From Compliance to Commitment’. It is being organised by the School of Business Environment, IICA, and will bring together senior representatives of Government, the corporate sector, Central Public Sector Enterprises, corporate foundations, implementing agencies, United Nations agencies, academic institutions and State Governments.

Along with five High Level Panels and a Fireside Chat spread across 2 days, the National Exhibition on CSR 2026 will also be held alongside the Conference, featuring 30–40 stalls organised around four thematic zones aligned with the Viksit Bharat @ 2047 vision: Yuva (education, skilling and employability), Garib (aspirational districts, tribal and marginalised communities), Annadata (agriculture and rural livelihoods) and Nari Shakti.

For further details, visit: https://iica.nic.in/csrconference/.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Union Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi to Inaugurate Windergy India 2026 in Chennai
8th edition of Windergy India to be held from October 7th –9th, 2026
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Education and Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Shri Pralhad Joshi, will inaugurate the 8th edition of Windergy India on October 8th, 2026, at the Chennai Trade Centre, setting in motion India's premier wind energy show.

Establishing a high-level strategic tone for the three-day event, the grand inauguration ceremony will be graced by Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for New and Renewable Energy and Power, and Thiru. C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar, Minister for Energy Resources and Law, Govt. of Tamil Nadu. The event will also have presence of senior officials from central & state governments, wind energy associations and industry icons.

The inauguration will feature global MoU announcements and the launch of key sectoral reports, alongside recognition of states demonstrating leadership in the wind energy sector.

India added a record 6.05 GW of wind capacity in FY2025-26, with cumulative capacity reaching 58.52 GW by August 2026. With 28 GW under implementation supporting the goal of 100 GW by 2030.

Running from October 7th–9th, 2026, Windergy India 2026 will comprise a 3-Day Trade Fair, 2-Day Conference, Technical Sessions, Round Tables, Live Demonstrations, B2B & B2G Meetings and Academia Connect. The landmark edition will serve as the definitive global epicenter for the wind energy sector, bringing together around 400 global exhibitors from over 20 countries alongside 500 delegates, further elevated by dedicated country pavilions from Denmark, Germany, and Spain.

The event will highlight domestic value addition, advanced next-gen turbine platforms, heavy-duty gearboxes, AI-driven O&M, and offshore wind capabilities. The conference will feature parallel high-level deliberations on policy frameworks, manufacturing competitiveness, repowering strategies, and offshore wind frontiers.

The event is being organised by the Indian Wind Turbine Manufacturers Association (IWTMA) and PDA Ventures Pvt. Ltd. with support from the MNRE and MoP. The inauguration will underscore a unified national and international commitment to scaling India’s renewable capacities.

Shri Durgesh Barkhane , a resident of Junardev, Chhindwara,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Unemployment to Self-Reliance
Chhindwara, MP’s Durga’s Journey towards Economic Independence
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 5:08PM by PIB Delhi

Financial assistance can play an important role in helping individuals from disadvantaged communities establish sustainable livelihoods and improve their economic condition. Timely support for self-employment can provide opportunities to create income sources, strengthen family financial security and promote greater self-reliance.

Shri Durgesh Barkhane, a resident of Junardev, Chhindwara, Madhya Pradesh, was selected under the NSFDC Electric Auto-Rickshaw Subsidy Scheme, 2024 and received financial assistance of Rs. 1,85,000. The assistance enabled him to acquire an auto-rickshaw and establish a source of livelihood for himself and his family.

Before receiving the assistance, Shri Durgesh was unemployed and had no stable source of income. Limited financial resources made it difficult for him to meet the basic needs of his family and maintain a secure livelihood.

With the financial assistance received under the scheme, he purchased an auto-rickshaw for approximately Rs. 15,000–20,000 and began earning through its operation. The livelihood opportunity has improved his financial condition and brought a noticeable positive change in his life. He is now able to contribute towards his family’s sustenance and well-being with greater dignity and confidence.

The assistance has provided Shri Durgesh with an opportunity to pursue self-employment and move towards greater financial stability. His experience demonstrates how timely financial support can create livelihood opportunities and help individuals become economically self-reliant.

Shri Barkhane expressed his heart, “The financial assistance gave me an opportunity to become self-reliant through an auto-rickshaw. It has improved my financial condition and enabled me to support my family with greater dignity.”

Shri Durgesh Barkhane’s journey demonstrates how financial assistance can transform livelihood prospects, strengthen family security and inspire others in rural communities to pursue self-employment and move towards self-reliance.

****

SS-113-TAR-KV-GA-RK

Dr. Jitendra Singh Reiterates Commitment to Ease of Life for Pensioners; Calls for Wider Adoption of Digital Pension Services
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Chairs 17th All India 'Pension Adalat'; 897 Long-Pending Cases Taken Up for Resolution, 756 (84.2%) resolved: Minister lauds PM Sh Narendra Modi for introducing the concept of Pension Adalat in 2017
Pension Reforms Must Remain Focused on Ease of Life and Last-Mile Delivery: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Dr. Jitendra Singh Highlights Technology-Enabled Pension Services, Digital Life Certificates and Family Pension Reforms
Government Working to Make Pension Services More Accessible, Technology-Driven and Citizen-Centric: Dr. Jitendra Singh
17th Pension Adalat Focuses on Expeditious Grievance Redressal and Pensioners’ Welfare; 756 of 897 Grievances Redressed, Achieving 84.2% Redressal Rate
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 5:05PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and Minister of State for PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today reiterated the Government’s commitment to ensuring Ease of Life and Pensioners’ Welfare, stressing that technology and digital interventions must ultimately translate into simpler and more accessible services for pensioners and their families.

Addressing the 17th Pension Adalat organised by the Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW) at T. N. Chaturvedi Memorial Hall, IIPA, New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that pension administration must continuously learn from the experiences and difficulties faced by pensioners and work towards removing shortcomings in the existing system. At today's Adalat 756 of 897 grievances were redressed, thus achieving 84.2% redressal rate. he Minister lauded PM Sh Narendra Modi for introducing the concept of Pension Adalat in 2017.

The Minister emphasised the importance of identifying gaps in pension delivery and addressing them through continuous improvement. He said that the objective of pension reforms is not merely technological advancement but ensuring that the benefits of reforms reach the last mile and make a tangible difference to pensioners.

The 17th Pension Adalat took up 897 grievances relating to family pensioners and super-senior pensioners for expeditious redressal. As on October 5, 2026, 756 cases have been redressed, registering a redressal rate of 84.2 per cent. The remaining cases are being pursued for redressal in the coming days, reflecting the Government’s continued focus on timely grievance resolution and Pensioners’ Welfare.

Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted the growing use of digital technology in pension-related services and said that efforts are being made to make processes simpler through digital identity and face-recognition based mechanisms. He stressed the need to continuously inform pensioners about such facilities so that they can make full use of the available digital services.

Referring to the Digital Life Certificate initiative, the Minister underlined the importance of campaigns and awareness programmes to ensure that pensioners are able to obtain digital certificates conveniently. He noted the significant scale achieved through such initiatives and stressed that greater awareness and outreach would further strengthen their impact.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the role of media and public communication in taking pension reforms to pensioners across the country. Referring to the positive results achieved through earlier awareness campaigns, he called for continued efforts to use modern communication tools to ensure that pensioners and their families remain informed about available services and reforms.

The Minister further said that technology should be used not only for routine service delivery but also for identifying issues and improving the overall pension administration system. He said that wherever gaps or avoidable difficulties are noticed, they should be reported and addressed so that the system can continuously improve.

Dr. Jitendra Singh stressed that Pensioners’ Welfare remains central to the Government’s approach and that technological interventions should be accompanied by sensitivity towards the needs of pensioners and family pensioners.

The Minister also referred to the continuing efforts to simplify pension-related procedures and improve support for families of pensioners. He emphasised that reforms must remain focused on practical difficulties faced by beneficiaries and should contribute to greater Ease of Life.

The 17th Pension Adalat brought pensioners and concerned Ministries and Departments together for the presentation and consideration of pension grievances. The programme included the presentation of cases before Dr. Jitendra Singh by the Joint Secretary (Pension). The proceedings enabled grievances to be examined directly and facilitated coordinated efforts towards their expeditious redressal.

During the adalat, Flyers on Success Stories of the 16th Pension Adalat and the e-booklet “Bringing Ease in the Life of Family Pensioners” were released. The publications highlight the Government’s continuing efforts towards effective grievance redressal and improving the experience of pensioners and family pensioners.

The 17th Pension Adalat is part of the institutional mechanism developed by the Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare for the meaningful, accessible and expeditious redressal of pensioners’ grievances.

An exemplary case of Ms. Chander Kanta Jally, whose husband made the supreme sacrifice in 1973. She was sanctioned Liberalised Family Pension. However, due to certain reasons, the family pension paid to her was lower than the amount to which she was entitled. She became aware of this and approached various forums. During the Pension Adalat, Sh. Jaswinder Jally, her son, attended through video conferencing from Chandigarh and presented the grievance on behalf of his mother before the Hon’ble MoS (PP). The case was discussed at length. Subsequently, family pension arrears amounting to Rs. 2.02 crore were released.

Another case involving Ms. Damyanti Sinha, with the help of the Pension Adalat, pensionary benefits of more than Rs. 72 lakh were released.

Both these cases involved super-senior family pensioners.

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India to hold 'Open Hearing and Camp Sitting' at Patna to hear cases of alleged human rights violations in Bihar on 7th-8th October 2026
Concerned State authorities and complainants to be present during the proceedings
Issues concerning human rights to be discussed with senior officers of the State
Interaction with representatives of civil society, NGOs and Human Rights Defenders also scheduled
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India is holding a two-day ‘Open Hearing and Camp Sitting’ at Gyan Bhawan, Patna, Bihar on 7th - 8th October 2026 to hear cases of alleged human rights violations in the State.

On Day-1, NHRC Chairperson, Justice V. Ramasubramanian and Members, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi and Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani will hear cases in the Full Commission sitting in the presence of complainants and concerned officers of the State.

The next day, on 8th October 2026, the Commission will hear cases in two separate Benches. The Chairperson will hear cases of alleged bonded labour. Simultaneously, a Division Bench, comprising Members, Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi and Smt. Vijaya Bharathi Sayani, will hear cases related to compliance matters and other complaints of alleged violation of human rights.

Thereafter, the Commission will interact with representatives of civil society organisations, NGOs and Human Rights Defenders. In the concluding session, the Commission will hold a meeting of senior officers to discuss important human rights issues pertaining to the State.

The NHRC, India has been holding Camp Sittings from time to time in various States since 2007 to facilitate easy access to justice for the victims of human rights violations.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Dr. Jitendra Singh Reviews Progress of Special Campaign 6 at DARPG Office, Sardar Patel Bhawan, New Delhi
Special Campaign 6 Goes Beyond Cleanliness to Promote Efficiency, Sustainability and the Vision of ‘Waste to Wealth’, says the Minister
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 4:52PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology; Earth Sciences; MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh visited the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) office at Sardar Patel Bhawan, New Delhi, on 5 October, 2026 to review the progress of Special Campaign 6, aimed at institutionalising Swachhata, reducing pendency and promoting efficient use of resources across Government offices.

The Minister reviewed the progress of the campaign along with Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, DARPG, Shri Puneet Yadav, Additional Secretary, Shri Avanish Kumar Mishra, Joint Secretary, and other senior officers. The campaign, aligned with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a Clean India, reinforces the Government’s commitment to Swachhata and good governance.

During the visit, Dr. Jitendra Singh directed officials to accelerate the transition from physical records to e-files under Special Campaign 6. Stressing efficiency, transparency and ease of access, he called for the swift digitisation of records and improved record management practices for better governance and more efficient office functioning.

In his remarks, Dr Jitendra Singh emphasized that the recycling of e-waste and other scrap also contributes to the Government’s broader vision of “Waste to Wealth” and promotes the principles of recycling and a Circular Economy, under which resources are recovered and put to productive use instead of being allowed to accumulate as waste.

The campaign’s thrust areas are being monitored through a single digital platform and include scientific e-waste disposal, timely resolution of pending matters such as MPs’ References, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO and IMC References and State Government References, improved record management, file disposal, and office cleanliness drives coupled with space optimisation for enhanced efficiency and sustainability, he underscored.

Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated the efforts of DARPG, the nodal department for conducting the Special Campaign, in institutionalising the campaign since 2021. He noted that Special Campaign 6 goes beyond cleanliness and has emerged as a comprehensive effort to strengthen governance, improve administrative efficiency and promote sustainable practices across Government offices.

Reflecting on the activities undertaken from 2nd October 2026, the Minister underlined the enduring relevance of Mahatma Gandhi’s vision of cleanliness and its integration with administrative reforms. He emphasised that cleanliness and efficiency must become sustained practices in everyday governance and public service.

He further emphasised that the campaign represents a collective responsibility of citizens and institutions. Every individual, office and community has a role to play in promoting cleanliness, efficiency and sustainable practices as part of the larger mission of nation-building.

Through Special Campaign 6, Government offices are not only becoming cleaner and more organised but are also improving workplace efficiency, reclaiming valuable space, reducing pendency, promoting recycling and ensuring that waste is put to productive use wherever possible. The campaign continues to drive Government institutions towards greater administrative efficiency, sustainable practices and a cleaner, more responsive governance framework.

A key focus of the campaign is the identification and reclamation of spaces occupied by unused material and discarded items. At DARPG, a space that had been lying unused and filled with junk has been completely cleared and transformed into a spacious common room for the convenience and welfare of employees. Such initiatives demonstrate how the campaign is helping convert underutilised spaces into productive and employee-friendly facilities.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Constraints to Academic Aspirations
Faridabad Haryana’s Dr. Pratibha Rani’s Journey through NFSC
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 4:37PM by PIB Delhi

Financial support can play an important role in enabling students from disadvantaged communities to pursue higher education and realise their academic aspirations. Timely fellowship assistance can help overcome financial barriers, strengthen educational opportunities and encourage greater participation in advanced studies.

Ms. Pratibha Rani, aged 35, from Faridabad, Haryana, received support under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste (NFSC) Scheme. Her fellowship assistance began in September 2019 and included Fellowship, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and Contingency support. She received approximately Rs. 18 lakh under the scheme, which helped her pursue her Ph.D. and overcome the financial constraints associated with higher education.

Before availing the fellowship, Pratibha faced financial challenges and limited awareness regarding educational support schemes. She felt that higher education for women from the Scheduled Caste community could often seem like a distant dream due to financial difficulties, family circumstances and peer pressure. The lack of awareness and limited interest in girls’ higher education within the community added to these barriers.

The NFSC fellowship provided Pratibha with financial stability and enabled her to focus on her academic goals. The support also helped strengthen her family’s financial position, particularly as her parents are retired. Alongside her academic journey, she has contributed to the education of underprivileged children for around 12 years, reflecting her commitment to making education more accessible to others.

Extending her gratitude for receiving financial support, Ms Pratibha said, “The NFSC fellowship helped me overcome financial challenges and achieve my dream of higher education. It gave me financial stability and encouraged me to contribute towards the education of underprivileged children.”

Her academic and professional journey also opened new opportunities. She joined a project at CSIR-National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi, where she received Rs. 43,000 per month for one year. The experience added to her professional exposure and helped improve her financial circumstances.

Pratibha’s journey demonstrates how targeted fellowship support can help talented students overcome financial barriers and pursue higher education. Her achievement has also motivated girls in her community to consider higher education and aspire towards professional and academic growth. Today, she takes pride in being professionally recognised as Dr. Pratibha Rani, reflecting the fulfilment of her dream of higher education and research.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri to mark delivery of 2,000th aero-engine at HAL Koraput tomorrow
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 4:35PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh will inaugurate the milestone event marking the delivery of the 2,000th aero-engine by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Koraput Division, in Odisha on October 06, 2026. The event will mark nearly six decades of HAL Koraput’s contribution to India’s aerospace and defence manufacturing capabilities and operational readiness of the Armed Forces.

The event will also highlight the establishment of a second production line for Shakti engines, with an investment of ₹218 crore. The additional capacity will support the growing requirements of indigenous helicopter platforms, including the Dhruv Advanced Light Helicopter and Prachand Light Combat Helicopter.

The event underlines the Government’s vision of transforming India from a buyer of defence equipment into a designer, developer and manufacturer of defence systems. Building indigenous aero-engine capability is a critical component of this vision, given the strategic importance and technological complexity of propulsion systems.

Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Defence Production) and Shri Ravi K, CMD, HAL would attend the event, among others.

Following the notable achievements of Special Campaign 5.0 last year, the Department has embarked upon the groundwork for the preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6.0, with a focused commitment to ensuring the responsible…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Department of Sports to participate in Special Campaign 6.0 to enhance cleanliness and resolve pending matters
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Sports, Government of India continues to set a benchmark in fostering responsible governance and streamlining administrative processes.

Following the notable achievements of Special Campaign 5.0 last year, the Department has embarked upon the groundwork for the preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6.0, with a focused commitment to ensuring the responsible governance, streamlining administrative processes and scientific e- waste management with the objective of “Effective Collection, Segregation and Disposal” of e-waste.

The Department, in collaboration with organizations under it - including the Sports Authority of India (SAI), Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE), National Sports University (NSU), National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA), and the National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL) diligently fulfilled the various targets set under the Special Campaign 5.0 last year, with senior officers actively overseeing the progress at each step. On the ground, cleanliness drives were carried out across 50 identified sites spanning field offices and headquarters of the organizations under this Department.

This concerted effort had resulted in the reclamation of 3,90,000 square feet of space, with many newly available areas repurposed into valuable utility spaces. In addition, scrap disposal during the campaign had generated Rs. 4,07,55,976 in revenue, underscoring a commitment to sustainability and resourcefulness in the pursuit of cleanliness. The Department and Organizations under it amplified the campaign’s reach and visibility by leveraging various social media platforms.

The Department is undertaking the Preparatory Phase (15th September - 30th September 2026) of the Special Campaign 6.0. The Department of Sports stands well-prepared to execute Special Campaign 6.0 with utmost effectiveness, aiming to establish higher standards in workplace cleanliness and to achieve the objectives outlined by DARPG.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh to Launch First Fleet Support Ship (FSS-1), Lay Keel of FSS-5 and Inaugurate Upgraded Slipway-4 & 300-Tonne Goliath Crane at Visakhapatnam
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant demonstration of India’s indigenous shipbuilding capabilities, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh will launch Fleet Support Ship-1 (FSS-1), lay the keel of Fleet Support Ship-5 (FSS-5) and also inaugurate the upgraded Slipway-4 and 300-tonne Goliath Crane at Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Vishakapatanam, on October 06, 2026.

The upgraded Slipway-4, with its extended length and enhanced load-bearing capability, supported by the 300-tonne Goliath Crane, will enable the shipyard to build and launch vessels of up to 45,000 DWT, significantly expanding its capacity to undertake large and complex platforms.

FSS-1, the first of five Fleet Support Ships being built for the Indian Navy, will enter the waters of the Bay of Bengal just 18 months after steel cutting. These 43,500-tonne vessels will replenish warships at sea, extending the Navy’s endurance and reach across the Indian Ocean Region. The keel laying of FSS-5 will mark the programme’s steady march towards series production.

The events will be attended by Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu, Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff, Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary (Defence Production), among others.

item.title: Integrated Ayurveda-Yoga Approach Shows Encouraging Results in Management of Bedwetting Among Children: ITRA Study
item.dc:creator: AYUSH
item.description: AYUSH Integrated Ayurveda-Yoga Approach Shows Encouraging Results in Management of Bedwetting Among Children: ITRA Study Combination of Ayurvedic medicine and yoga asanas reported up to 70% improvement in nocturnal enuresis Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi A clinical study conducted at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, has reported encouraging results from an integrated approach combining Ayurvedic medicine with yoga asanas in the…
item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
Integrated Ayurveda-Yoga Approach Shows Encouraging Results in Management of Bedwetting Among Children: ITRA Study
Combination of Ayurvedic medicine and yoga asanas reported up to 70% improvement in nocturnal enuresis
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi

A clinical study conducted at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, has reported encouraging results from an integrated approach combining Ayurvedic medicine with yoga asanas in the management of nocturnal enuresis, commonly known as bedwetting, among children.

The eight-week study involving approximately 38 children in the age group of 6–14 years found that children receiving Ayurvedic medicine along with regular practice of selected yoga asanas showed greater improvement compared to those receiving Ayurvedic medicine alone. The findings have been published in the internationally recognised AYU Journal.

Study Conducted in Two Groups

The study was conducted by the Department of Kaumarbhritya (Paediatrics), ITRA, Jamnagar. The participating children were divided into two groups.

Group 1 – Ayurvedic Medicine Alone:
Children received Medhya Rasayana Churna, a formulation comprising Brahmi, Shankhpushpi, Yashtimadhu (liquorice) and Guduchi, administered twice daily with milk.

Group 2 – Ayurvedic Medicine with Yoga:
Children received the same Ayurvedic formulation along with four yoga asanas — Utkatasana, Ardha-Shalabhasana, Bhujangasana and Shavasana — practised regularly in the morning and evening.

Significant Improvement Reported

The study reported encouraging outcomes across several parameters:

Reduction in bedwetting: Children receiving the Ayurvedic formulation alone showed approximately 38% improvement in the frequency of bedwetting, while those receiving the combined intervention of Ayurveda and yoga showed approximately 70% improvement.

Improvement in memory: An approximately 61% improvement in memory was reported among children receiving the combined intervention, compared to around 31% among those receiving the Ayurvedic medicine alone.

Reduction in irritability: Children in the combined intervention group showed approximately 66% reduction in irritability, along with improvements in behavioural parameters.

Reduction in hyperactivity: Regular yoga practice was associated with approximately 71% reduction in hyperactivity, with encouraging improvements also observed in concentration and morale.

The research paper was conducted and presented by Prof. Vaidya Virendra Kori, Vaidya Sagar Bhinde and Vaidya Amisha Bavarva. The researchers undertook a detailed analysis of the data generated during the study, following which the research paper was accepted for publication in the AYU Journal.

According to Prof. Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, Jamnagar, nocturnal enuresis may, in some cases, be associated with difficulties in bladder control as well as psychological and behavioural factors.

The study indicates that selected yoga practices, including Utkatasana and Bhujangasana, may support strengthening of the pelvic region and better bladder control. Ayurvedic ingredients such as Brahmi and Shankhpushpi have traditionally been used for their calming properties and their role in supporting mental well-being.

The findings highlight the potential of an integrated approach combining Ayurveda and yoga in the management of nocturnal enuresis among children. The study also underlines the importance of integrating appropriate lifestyle practices with traditional systems of medicine for promoting overall health and well-being.

It may be noted that bedwetting is a common condition among children and should be addressed with sensitivity and appropriate medical guidance.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister’s Press Statement during Joint Press Statement with the President of Switzerland
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 2:26PM by PIB Delhi

Your Excellency, Mr President,
दोनों देशों के delegates,
मीडिया के साथियों,

नमस्कार!

स्विट्ज़रलैंड के राष्ट्रपति जी का भारत में हार्दिक स्वागत करते हुए मुझे बहुत खुशी हो रही है।

सबसे पहले, मैं भारत-स्विट्ज़रलैंड संबंधों के प्रति उनकी प्रतिबद्धता की सराहना करता हूँ। पिछले वर्ष अक्टूबर में, उनके व्यक्तिगत समर्थन से, हमने भारत और यूरोपियन फ्री ट्रेड एसोसिएशन, यानि “एफ्टा” देशों के बीच, एक ऐतिहासिक ट्रैड एण्ड इकनॉमिक पार्ट्नर्शिप एग्रीमेंट लागू किया। यह यूरोप के किसी भी economic bloc के साथ भारत का पहला FTA है।

यह इनवेस्टमेंट, इनोवेशन, jobs और साझा समृद्धि का ऐम्बिशस ब्लूप्रिन्ट भी है। इससे हम अगले 15 वर्षों में भारत में 100 बिलियन डॉलर का इनवेस्टमेंट, और 10 लाख डायरेक्ट जॉब्स के लक्ष्यों को साकार करेंगे।

Friends,

भारत और स्विट्ज़रलैंड की मित्रता सदियों पुरानी है। उन्नीसवीं सदी में स्वामी विवेकानंद ने, स्विस आल्प्स में हिमालय की झलक देखी थी। महात्मा गांधी ने भी स्विट्ज़रलैंड में समय बिताया और वहाँ के लोगों से संवाद किया। इन ऐतिहासिक यात्राओं की स्मृतियाँ आज भी हमारी मित्रता में गूंजती हैं।

आज, इनोवेशन, इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर और एडवांस्ड टेक्नॉलजी हमारी partnership के मजबूत स्तंभ हैं। और आज की इस समिट से हम अपनी साझेदारी को एक नई गति और नई ऊँचाई देने जा रहे हैं।

Friends,

हमने भारत के exports का स्विट्ज़रलैंड में मार्केट एक्सेस बढ़ाने, और दोनों देशों के बीच इनवेस्टमेंट को और सुगम बनाने के लिए कई महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय लिए हैं।

इससे भारत के ऐग्रिकल्चर, फार्मा, textile और engineering goods की स्विट्ज़रलैंड में निर्यात बढ़ेगी। और साथ-साथ, भारत के बायोटेक, लाइफ साइंसेज़, बैंकिंग, इन्श्योरेन्स, फूड प्रोसेसिंग और सस्टे-निबिलिटी जैसे महत्वपूर्ण क्षेत्रों में हम नए स्विस इनवेस्टमेंट को आकर्षित करेंगे। इन पहलों से हम साथ मिलकर पूरे विश्व के लिए trusted supply chains और रिलायबल सोल्युशंस विकसित करेंगे।

Friends,

आज हमने मिलिटरी एक्सचेंज और defense production में सहयोग की नई संभावनाओं की पहचान की। नूक्लीअर एनर्जी में सहयोग को और प्रगाढ़ करने पर भी सहमति बनी।

वाराणसी का रोप-वे, नोएडा का जेवर एयरपोर्ट, और पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में railways तथा tunnelling प्रोजेक्ट्स, हमारे इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर सहयोग के उज्ज्वल उदाहरण हैं। इस सहयोग को सुदृढ़ करने के लिए आज हमने ट्रांसपोर्ट, मोबिलिटी और इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर पर एग्रीमेंट किया है।

हम स्विट्ज़रलैंड की इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर कम्पनीज़ को भारत में बड़े लेवल पर निवेश करने, और कपैसिटी बिल्डिंग, डिजाइन और मैन्युफैक्चरिंग में भागीदारी के लिए आमंत्रित करते हैं।

Friends,

साइंस और टेक्नॉलजी सहयोग भी हमारी साझेदारी का एक मजबूत स्तम्भ है। मुझे बहुत खुशी है कि हम जल्द ही हेल्थ, क्लीन एनर्जी और स्पेस जैसे priority areas में नए जॉइंट रिसर्च प्रॉजेक्ट लॉन्च करने जा रहे हैं। हम भारत के साइंस स्टार्ट-अप्स की कपैसिटी बिल्डिंग के लिए ज़ूरिक यूनिवर्सिटी के साथ हुए एग्रीमेंट का भी हम स्वागत करते हैं।

स्विट्ज़रलैंड में योग और आयुर्वेद की बढ़ती हुई लोकप्रियता को देखते हुए, आज हमने इन क्षेत्रों में सहयोग प्रगाढ़ करने पर भी सार्थक चर्चा की।

Friends,

people-to-people ties हमारी पार्ट्नर्शिप की सबसे बड़ी ताकत है। आज हुए माइग्रेशन और मोबिलिटी पार्ट्नर्शिप एग्रीमेंट और यंग प्रोफेशनल्स एग्रीमेंट से, भारत के students, researchers, professionals और युवाओं के लिए स्विट्ज़रलैंड में कई नए अवसर खुलेंगे।

Friends,

भारत और स्विट्ज़रलैंड, दोनों डेमॉक्रैटिक वैल्यूस, rule of law, डायलॉग और डिप्लोमसी में विश्वास रखते हैं। हम ग्लोबल पीस और स्टेबिलिटी के लिए मिलकर काम करते रहेंगे।

यूक्रेन हो या पश्चिमी एशिया, भारत शांति की दिशा में किए जाने वाले हर सार्थक प्रयास का समर्थन करता रहा है।

हम इस बात पर भी एकमत हैं, कि बढ़ते हुए ग्लोबल challenges के समाधान के लिए Global institutions में रिफॉर्म अनिवार्य है।

Friends,

मैं स्विट्ज़रलैंड के प्रेसीडेंट का आभारी हूँ, कि वे एक बड़े बिजनेस delegation के साथ भारत आए हैं। 7 अक्टूबर को हम उनकी उपस्थिति में भारत-एफ्टा बिजनेस लीडर्स के साथ “प्रॉस्पेरिटी समिट” आयोजित करने जा रहे हैं। यह समिट हमारे ट्रेड और इनवेस्टमेंट पार्ट्नर्शिप के promise को concrete outcomes में बदलने का एक महत्वपूर्ण मंच बनेगी। मैं इस समिट में भाग लेने वाले सभी बिजनेस लीडर्स को भी बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं देता हूँ।

Your Excellency,

इस वर्ष फ़रवरी में भारत ने विश्व की सबसे बड़ी AI समिट का आयोजन किया। अगले वर्ष स्विट्ज़रलैंड “जिनेवा AI समिट” के माध्यम से इस यात्रा को आगे बढ़ाएगा। जिनेवा AI समिट की सफलता के लिए मैं स्विट्ज़रलैंड को हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं देता हूँ। मुझे विश्वास है कि हम साथ मिलकर AI को responsible, inclusive और human-centric बनाने की दिशा में आगे बढ़ते रहेंगे।

एक बार फिर, भारत की इस यात्रा के लिए, और भारत-स्विट्ज़रलैंड संबंधों के प्रबल समर्थक रहने के लिए, आपका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

 

****

MJPS/SS/ST

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Saving Time, Shortening Journeys
How India’s Infrastructure Is Bringing Places Closer
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 12:37PM by PIB Delhi

 Connectivity Measured in Hours Saved

For millions of travellers, better connectivity is measured in hours saved, not only in kilometres built. Across India, new bridges, tunnels, expressways and rail services are changing the time it takes to travel between cities, regions and communities. By replacing detours, difficult terrain and slow routes with direct and faster connections, these projects are making infrastructure-led transformation visible in everyday travel. As faster links reach more parts of the country, distance is becoming less of a constraint on everyday mobility.

 

 Bridges: Crossing Barriers, Cutting Travel Time

Bridges are removing long and slow river crossings from everyday travel and turning journeys that once took hours into much shorter trips.

  • Bhupen Hazarika Setu/ Dhola–Sadiya Bridge, Assam–Arunachal Pradesh ( May, 2017)

6 hours → 1 hour

Travel time between Rupai in Assam and Meka/Roing in Arunachal Pradesh has fallen from six hours to one hour, saving five hours.

  • Bogibeel Bridge, Assam (December, 2018)

A day-long journey → 1–2 hours

The rail-cum-road bridge over the Brahmaputra has transformed connectivity between Dhemaji and Dibrugarh. Journeys that earlier took almost an entire day now take about one to two hours.

  • Atal Setu, Maharashtra (January, 2024)

2 hours → 20 minutes

The Mumbai Trans Harbour Link provides a direct connection between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai, cutting the journey to about 20 minutes.

  • Kosi Rail Mahasetu, Bihar (September, 2020)

8 hours → 30 minutes

The Kosi Rail Mahasetu reduced the rail journey between Nirmali and Saraigarh from about eight hours to 30 minutes, while reducing the distance from about 300 km to 22 km.

  • Sisseri River Bridge, Arunachal Pradesh (November, 2019)

About 5 hours saved

The 200-metre Sisseri River Bridge reduced the travel time between Pasighat and Roing by about five hours, strengthening connectivity between Dibang Valley and Siang.

 

 Tunnels: Cutting Through Terrain, Saving Hours

Tunnels are taking the shortest route through some of India’s most difficult terrain. Bypassing mountains, winding roads and vulnerable stretches, they are bringing down travel times while making journeys seamless.

  • Atal Tunnel, Himachal Pradesh (October, 2020)

4–5 hours saved

The 9.02-km tunnel bypasses Rohtang Pass and reduces the Manali–Sarchu distance by 46 km, providing all-weather connectivity to Lahaul-Spiti.

  • Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel, Jammu & Kashmir (April, 2017)

Nearly 2 hours saved

The 9-km tunnel bypasses difficult terrain, cuts the travel distance by about 30 km and reduces travel time between Jammu and Srinagar by nearly two hours.

  • Banihal–Qazigund Road Tunnel, Jammu & Kashmir (April, 2022)

~1.5 hours saved

The 8.45-km twin-tube tunnel cuts the road distance by 16 km and reduces journey time by around one and a half hours.

  • Sela Tunnel, Arunachal Pradesh (March, 2024)

Travel time cut by over 1 hour

Built at an altitude of about 13,000 feet, the tunnel ensures all-weather connectivity on the strategically important Tezpur-Tawang route.

 

 Expressways & Economic Corridors

Expressways are changing the pace of inter-city travel through shorter alignments, controlled access and higher speeds. Long journeys that once consumed several hours are being compressed into significantly faster road trips.

  • Delhi–Meerut Expressway (2021)

2.5 hours → 50 minutes

The 82-km project reduced travel time between Delhi and Meerut from around two and a half hours to about 50 minutes.

  • Bengaluru–Mysuru Expressway (March, 2023)

3 hours → 75 minutes

The 118-km expressway has reduced travel time between Bengaluru and Mysuru from nearly three hours to about 75 minutes.

  • Delhi–Dehradun Economic Corridor (April, 2026)

6 hours → 2.5 hours

The 213-km access-controlled corridor reduces travel time between Delhi and Dehradun from over six hours to around two and a half hours.

  • Mumbai–Nagpur Samruddhi Mahamarg (December, 2022)

16 hours → ~8 hours

The 701-km access-controlled expressway has substantially reduced travel time between Mumbai and Nagpur.

  • Ahmedabad–Dholera Expressway (March, 2026)

Ahmedabad- Dholera: from 100 km & 2 hr 15 min → 83 km & 45 min
Ahmedabad to Bhavnagar: from 169 km & 3 hr 15 min → 141 km & 1 hr 45 min

The access-controlled greenfield expressway stretching over 109 km provides a high-speed link between Ahmedabad and Dholera.

  • Delhi–Amritsar–Katra Expressway (Phase-I- July, 2026)

Delhi–Amritsar: 8 hours → 4 hours
Delhi–Katra: 14 hours → 6 hours

The expressway is being developed to boost pilgrim and tourist traffic to Shri Mata Vaishno Devi, and catalyse industrial and logistics development along the corridor.

  • Delhi–Mumbai Expressway

33 hours → ~12 hours

The greenfield expressway is being developed to reduce travel time between Delhi and Mumbai to about 12 hours from roughly 33 hours.

 

 

 Railways: Faster Trains, Shorter Journeys

New-generation trains and dedicated high-speed corridors are bringing major time savings to rail travel. The 2026 railway timetable reflects this shift, with 549 trains speeded up across the network. Of these, 20 trains became faster by 60 minutes or more. Another 48 trains gained 31–59 minutes, while 105 trains gained 16–30 minutes. The remaining 376 trains were speeded up by 5–15 minutes.

New Generation Trains

  • Vande Bharat Express, New Delhi–Varanasi (February, 2019)

40–50% faster than earlier services

India's first Vande Bharat was launched on 15 February 2019 on the New Delhi–Kanpur–Prayagraj–Varanasi corridor. The scheduled travel time between New Delhi and Varanasi is approximately eight hours, making it around 40-50% faster than earlier services on the route.

  • Vande Bharat Express, Katra–Srinagar (June, 2025)

2–3 hours saved

The train cut Katra–Srinagar travel to about three hours. The extended Jammu–Srinagar service now covers the journey in 4 hours 50 minutes.

  • Vande Bharat Express, Banaras–Khajuraho (November, 2025)

~2 hours 40 minutes saved

The train saves about 2 hours 40 minutes compared with the special trains earlier in operation.

  • Vande Bharat Express, Ernakulam–Bengaluru (November, 2025)

Over 2 hours saved

The service covers the journey in 8 hours 40 minutes, reducing travel time by over two hours.

  • Vande Bharat Express, Lucknow–Saharanpur (November, 2025)

Nearly 1 hour saved

The train completes the journey in approximately 7 hours 45 minutes.

  • Vande Bharat Sleeper, Howrah–Guwahati (January, 2026)

~17 hours → ~14 hours

India's first Vande Bharat Sleeper saves nearly three hours over the Saraighat Express. It has 16 air-conditioned coaches for around 823 passengers.

 

High-Speed Rail Corridors

  • Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor

8–9 hours by road → ~1 hour 58 minutes

The 508-km corridor, with an operational speed of 320 kmph, will serve 12 stations. It includes India's first undersea rail tunnel, about 7 km beneath Thane Creek. The first service is targeted for August 2027.

  • Seven Announced High-Speed Rail (HSR) Corridors

Major city pairs within about 1–4 hours

Announced in the Union Budget 2026–27, the corridors span nearly 4,000 km with an estimated investment of ₹16 lakh crore.

 

Corridor

Indicative travel time

Delhi–Varanasi

~3 hours 50 minutes

Varanasi–Patna–Siliguri

~2 hours 55 minutes

Chennai–Bengaluru

~1 hour 13 minutes

Bengaluru–Hyderabad

~2 hours

Chennai–Hyderabad

~2 hours 55 minutes

Mumbai–Pune

~48 minutes

Pune–Hyderabad

~1 hour 55 minutes

 

 Hours Returned to Travellers and Communities

The transformation of India’s transport network is changing how people and regions connect with one another. Bridges and tunnels are opening new crossings while expressways and modern rail services are redefining long-distance travel. Together, these interventions are making mobility more seamless and expanding access across regions.

item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST signs agreement with BigEndian Semiconductors for ₹130 crore RDI support to develop indigenous AI Vision SoC Project VeerAI to advance secure, application-specific semiconductor technology from TRL-5 to TRL-9 Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 12:23PM by PIB Delhi Strengthening India’s efforts to build indigenous semiconductor capabilities for critical and emerging applications, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s BigEndian Semiconductors,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB-DST signs agreement with BigEndian Semiconductors for ₹130 crore RDI support to develop indigenous AI Vision SoC
Project VeerAI to advance secure, application-specific semiconductor technology from TRL-5 to TRL-9
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 12:23PM by PIB Delhi

Strengthening India’s efforts to build indigenous semiconductor capabilities for critical and emerging applications, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s BigEndian Semiconductors, Bengaluru, Karnataka for financial support of ₹130 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.

The project, Project VeerAI, has a total project cost of ₹260 crore and aims to take the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-5 to TRL-9. The financial support will be provided through Optional Convertible Debt (OCD). Project VeerAI seeks to develop a camera-focused AI Vision System-on-Chip (SoC) on a sovereign technology platform, addressing the growing requirement for secure, intelligent and application-specific semiconductor solutions.

The project is positioned around the development of a secure AI chip for surveillance applications, particularly CCTV systems, with the objective of reducing dependence on externally developed semiconductor and technology supply chains. The proposed platform is designed to combine AI processing and smart features with security, privacy and connectivity capabilities. The technology is being developed initially for CCTV and surveillance applications in India and the Global South, with a roadmap for deployment across multiple sectors. Beyond surveillance, the platform is envisaged for applications in defence, automotive, industrial and medical domains, creating a wider market for indigenous AI-enabled semiconductor solutions.

The project also seeks to leverage India’s growing VLSI design and semiconductor talent, translating domestic design capabilities into a scalable product platform. By focusing on application-specific SoCs rather than general-purpose chips, the programme aims to address specific industry requirements while enabling faster technology deployment and commercialisation. The development of indigenous AI and semiconductor technologies has growing significance as connected devices and intelligent systems become increasingly embedded across critical infrastructure. Secure and application-specific chips can play an important role in addressing requirements related to data security, privacy, device-level intelligence and technology sovereignty.

Through the RDI support, BigEndian Semiconductors will undertake further technology development, validation, integration, testing and scale-up activities required to progress Project VeerAI from TRL-5 to TRL-9.

Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said, “Semiconductors are foundational to almost every emerging technology, and building indigenous capabilities in application-specific AI chips is an important part of strengthening India’s technology ecosystem. The RDI Fund enables sustained support for technologies that require significant investment to move from advanced development to commercial deployment. The support to BigEndian Semiconductors reflects TDB’s focus on enabling Indian companies to develop strategic semiconductor capabilities and translate domestic design expertise into deployable products.”

Promoters of BigEndian Semiconductors said, “The RDI support from TDB will enable us to accelerate the development and validation of Project VeerAI and take our AI Vision SoC towards commercial readiness. Our focus is on building a secure, application-specific semiconductor platform that can address the requirements of surveillance and other critical sectors while leveraging India’s indigenous semiconductor design capabilities. This partnership will help us progress the technology towards TRL-9 and contribute to the development of a stronger domestic semiconductor ecosystem.”

***

item.title: Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the qualities of a noble-hearted person

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister shares Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the qualities of a noble-hearted person
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 10:14AM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting that purity of heart, a spirit of sacrifice, courage, equanimity in joy and sorrow, competence, affection and truthfulness are the defining qualities of a noble-hearted person and an exceptional personality.

The Prime Minister shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam-

“शुचित्वं त्यागिता शौर्यं सामान्यं सुखदुःखयोः।

दाक्षिण्यं चानुरक्तिश्च सत्यता च सुहृद्गुणाः॥”

The Subhashitam conveys that purity of heart, a spirit of sacrifice, courage, equanimity in both joy and sorrow, competence, affection and truthfulness-these are not merely the qualities of an ordinary friend but rather the defining traits of a person endowed with a noble heart and an exceptional personality.

The Prime Minister wrote on X;

“शुचित्वं त्यागिता शौर्यं सामान्यं सुखदुःखयोः।

दाक्षिण्यं चानुरक्तिश्च सत्यता च सुहृद्गुणाः॥”

 

शुचित्वं त्यागिता शौर्यं सामान्यं सुखदुःखयोः। दाक्षिण्यं चानुरक्तिश्च सत्यता च सुहृद्गुणाः॥ https://t.co/vKvqfnXsCm

item.dc:creator: Department of Atomic Energy
item.description: Department of Atomic Energy UCIL Celebrates Diamond Jubilee Year, Marks Six Decades of India’s Uranium Mining and Processing Capability Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 8:31AM by PIB Delhi Uranium Corporation of India Limited, a PSU under the Department of Atomic Energy, celebrated its Diamond Jubilee Year, marking six decades since its incorporation on 4 October 1967 and its contribution to India’s nuclear power programme Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance, Atomic Energy Commission, graced the celebrations at Jaduguda as the Chief Guest; she visited the Technology Demonstration…
item.content:encoded:
Department of Atomic Energy
UCIL Celebrates Diamond Jubilee Year, Marks Six Decades of India’s Uranium Mining and Processing Capability
Posted On: 05 OCT 2026 8:31AM by PIB Delhi
  • Uranium Corporation of India Limited, a PSU under the Department of Atomic Energy, celebrated its Diamond Jubilee Year, marking six decades since its incorporation on 4 October 1967 and its contribution to India’s nuclear power programme
  • Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance, Atomic Energy Commission, graced the celebrations at Jaduguda as the Chief Guest; she visited the Technology Demonstration Pilot Plant and the proposed new site of the Dark Matter Laboratory of the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, an aided institution of DAE
  • A first-of-its-kind Journalists’ Workshop provided the media delegates with an opportunity to gain first-hand experience of UCIL’s operations
  • A special DAE Technology Exhibition for the school students showcased the industrial and societal applications of nuclear energy
  • The celebrations showcased UCIL’s evolving capabilities in uranium mining and processing, while reflecting on its historical and continued contributions to India’s nuclear energy programme

The Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL), a Public Sector Enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), celebrated its Diamond Jubilee Year on 4 October 2026, marking six decades of its journey in uranium mining and processing and its contribution at the forefront of India’s nuclear power programme.

The Diamond Jubilee Year celebrations at Jaduguda brought together senior officials, scientists, engineers, technical personnel, employees, media professionals and other stakeholders to commemorate an important milestone in UCIL’s institutional journey and to look ahead to the opportunities and shared responsibilities of the future.

The Diamond Jubilee Year celebrations were graced by Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance, Atomic Energy Commission, as the Chief Guest. During the programme, she also visited the Technology Demonstration Pilot Plant (TDPP) at C, R&D, Jaduguda, and the proposed new site of the Dark Matter Laboratory at the 815-metre level of the Jaduguda underground mine.

Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance, Atomic Energy Commission, said, “The Diamond Jubilee Year of UCIL is a celebration of six decades of scientific capability, institutional experience and dedicated service to the nation. It is also an occasion to pay respectful homage to Dr Homi Jehangir Bhabha and the pioneers who laid the foundations of India’s uranium mining and processing capabilities. From the depths of the earth to the larger nuclear energy programme, UCIL has played an important and responsible role in building indigenous capability in uranium mining and processing. Over these six decades, generations of UCIL personnel have demonstrated remarkable dedication and grit, working in challenging conditions and environments to sustain this important national endeavour. As India looks towards an expanded role for nuclear energy, this milestone is also an opportunity to recognise the people, technologies and systems that have sustained this journey and to look ahead with confidence.”

Dr Ajit Kumar Mohanty, Secretary, Department of Atomic Energy and Chairman, Atomic Energy Commission, conveyed his greetings on the occasion and said, “The Diamond Jubilee Year is an occasion to recognise the contributions of UCIL and to reaffirm the importance of continued innovation and capability building as India advances on the Nuclear Energy Mission.”

A significant feature of the Diamond Jubilee Year programme was the Journalists’ Workshop, organised at the Information Centre, Narwapahar, along with a DAE Technology Exhibition showcasing technologies and applications emerging from the DAE’s Units and Institutions.

The workshop brought participating media delegates closer to the science, technology and people behind India’s nuclear power programme. It provided the media delegates with an opportunity to interact with scientists, engineers and technical experts and gain a deeper understanding of the technologies, systems and applications that constitute the wider nuclear and radiation technology ecosystem.

The media delegates visited UCIL’s uranium mining and milling facilities, gaining first-hand exposure to mining operations, ore handling and processing systems, as well as the technologies and practices adopted at the operational sites.

Dr. Kacham Anand Rao, Chairman & Managing Director, UCIL, said: “The Diamond Jubilee Year is a proud milestone for every member of the UCIL family. Over six decades, UCIL has steadily built expertise and infrastructure in uranium mining and processing, while strengthening its capabilities in technology, safety and environmental management. We were particularly pleased to open our operations and facilities to the media on this occasion. The Journalists’ Workshop and DAE Technology Expo provided an opportunity for first-hand engagement with the science, technology and people behind our operations and with the wider contributions of DAE.”

Established in 1967, UCIL has been an integral part of the development of India’s indigenous uranium mining and processing capabilities, providing the essential resource base for India’s nuclear power programme. The Diamond Jubilee Year celebrations marked the evolution of a specialised national capability, from underground and opencast mining to ore processing, technology development, occupational safety, radiation protection and environmental management.

Six decades of experience. A continuing commitment to capability. And a renewed journey towards the future of India’s nuclear energy programme. Uranium Leads the Way.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat Organises “Walk for Nasha Mukt Yuva” Nationwide
Over 1 Lakh Youth and Citizens Participate Across More Than 150 Locations
Posted On: 04 OCT 2026 11:26PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat” Abhiyan, MY Bharat and its partner organisations organised “Walk for Nasha Mukt Yuva” on October 4, 2026, across more than 150 locations nationwide, witnessing the enthusiastic participation of over 1 lakh youth and citizens.

The nationwide initiative aimed to create widespread awareness among youth and communities about the harmful effects of substance abuse and to promote healthy, responsible and addiction-free lifestyles. The programme brought together young people, citizens, public representatives and partner organisations to reinforce the message of collective responsibility in building a healthier and drug-free society.

As part of the initiative, participants took part in 3–5 km walks, Nukkad Nataks, slogan writing, heritage walks and other youth-led awareness activities. These activities used public spaces and community participation to spread awareness about the risks associated with substance abuse and encourage young people to make healthy and responsible lifestyle choices.

Several programmes also featured the Nasha Mukt Yuva Pledge, through which participants committed themselves to staying away from substance abuse and contributing towards creating a healthy, aware and drug-free society. The pledge further strengthened the campaign's emphasis on individual responsibility and collective action against substance abuse.

The nationwide programme also witnessed the participation of several public representatives and dignitaries, adding further momentum and visibility to the campaign. The key dignitaries who participated included 2 Lieutenant Governors, 1 Cabinet Minister, 8 Members of Parliament and 8 Members of Legislative Assemblies.

The enthusiastic participation of youth, citizens, public representatives and partner organisations across the country reflects the growing collective resolve to build a Nasha Mukt Yuva for a Viksit Bharat. The initiative reinforces the vision of empowering young people to lead healthier lives and become active contributors to a healthier, stronger and developed India.

The “Walk for Nasha Mukt Yuva” is part of the broader Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan, which seeks to mobilise youth and communities through sustained awareness, participation and collective action against substance abuse.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal to Flag Off First International Cargo Voyage from Dibrugarh
Maiden methanol voyage from Bogibeel to Dhaka via National Waterway-2 marks a new chapter for Assam's river trade since Independence
Posted On: 04 OCT 2026 9:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal, will flag off the first international cargo voyage from Dibrugarh tomorrow, 5 October 2026, at 11:00 AM at Bogibeel Terminal, Dibrugarh. The Chief Minister of Assam, Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, will join the ceremony virtually as Chief Guest.

The maiden voyage will carry methanol produced by Assam Petro-Chemicals Limited (APCL) from Bogibeel to Pangaon Port in Dhaka, Bangladesh, via National Waterway-2 (river Brahmaputra) and the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route (IBPR). It will be the first time since Independence that a cargo consignment sails from Dibrugarh to a foreign port.

For generations before Independence, the Brahmaputra was Upper Assam's main link to the markets of the world, and Dibrugarh was among the region's most important river ports. Tomorrow's flag-off marks the return of that link, reflecting the Government's push to develop inland waterways as a cheaper, greener and more efficient mode of transport for the Northeast.

The ceremony will be attended by Charan Boro, Minister of Transport, Government of Assam; Rameswar Teli, Minister of Labour Welfare, Government of Assam; and Bimal Borah, Minister of Industries, Commerce and Public Enterprises, Government of Assam, as Special Guests.

Presence of Terash Gowalla, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha); MLAs Prasanta Phukan (Dibrugarh), Chakradhar Gogoi (Khowang), Sanjoy Kishan (Makum), Suren Phukan (Digboi), Binod Hazarika (Chabua-Lahowal), Bhaskar Sharma (Margherita), Taranga Gogoi (Naharkatia) and Pulok Gohain (Tinsukia); Sushil Kumar Lohani, Chairman, Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI); and Bikul Ch. Deka, Chairman, APCL is also expected.

The event is being organised by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways and IWAI, together with the Government of Assam and APCL.

The ceremony will be streamed live on IWAI’s official YouTube channel, IWAI_ShipMin. More information on iwai.gov.in and through IWAI’s official social media handles on X, LinkedIn, Instagram and Facebook.
