item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) Rajasthan Unit observes National Anti-Drug Addiction Day with awareness programmes and cleanliness campaigns across opium cultivation areas on the birth anniversary of the Father of the Nation Shri Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 10:35PM by PIB Delhi

On the occasion of National Anti-Drug Addiction Day and the Birth Anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) Rajasthan Unit organised a series of Awareness Programmes in opium cultivation areas to sensitise cultivators and local communities about the harmful effects of drug abuse and promote the message of a drug-free India.

An awareness session on drug abuse and its adverse effects was organised at the University of Kota under Operation Yuva Raksha by Central Bureau of Narcotics, Kota.

The session was attended by Shri Murlidhar Pratihar, Registrar, University of Kota, NSS Head Ms. Shweta and faculty members and students were also present.  During the session, the Chief Guest, Shri Naresh Bundel, Deputy Narcotics Commissioner, Kota, interacted with the students and explained how even intelligent and well-informed individuals can be influenced through manipulation, peer pressure and social conditioning. Through practical examples, presentations and videos, he explained the concepts of Fast Mind and Slow Mind and how the first exposure to addictive substances can gradually lead towards repeated use, habit and dependence.

The students were encouraged to say “NO” at the very first instance, resist peer pressure and make informed and responsible choices. The session was highly interactive, with students actively participating and raising several thoughtful questions.

At the conclusion of the session, the participants took a Drug De-Addiction Pledge (Nasha Mukti Pledge), reaffirming their commitment to stay away from drugs and contribute towards a healthier and drug-free society.

The DOO, Kota, organised a programme for opium cultivators of Kota Division on the harmful effects of opium, cannabis and other illicit drugs. Banners carrying the campaign message were displayed and the programme concluded with the “Oath for an Addiction-Free India”, with participants pledging to spread awareness in their communities.

 

 

The DOO, Jhalawar, conducted a programme in a poppy cultivation village near Babrikhda, Tehsil Jhalrapatan, focusing on the adverse effects of substance abuse and community participation in preventing addiction.

The DOO, Bhilwara, organised a programme at Sawaipur-Badala Bypass Highway, which witnessed participation from hundreds of local residents and opium cultivators. The participants were encouraged to contribute towards creating a drug-free society.

The DOO, Chittorgarh-I, organised an Awareness and Cleanliness Campaign under the “Yuva Raksha and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan” at Menar Village, Tehsil Vallabhnagar, District Udaipur. The programme focused on healthy, drug-free lifestyles and included a cleanliness drive involving officials and local residents.

The DOO, Chittorgarh-III, organised a programme at Mangrol, a poppy cultivation village, highlighting the physical, psychological and social consequences of drug abuse. The activity was also included in the proceedings of the Gram Sabha.

 

 

The DOO, Pratapgarh-II, organised an Awareness and Cleanliness Campaign at Village Gomana, Chhoti Sadri, combining the message of cleanliness with prevention of drug abuse and promotion of healthy lifestyles.

ALL THE ABOVE PROGRAMMES emphasised that prevention of drug abuse requires active participation from all sections of society, particularly local communities and cultivators. Through these initiatives, CBN reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening awareness, community participation and collective action towards the vision of a drug-free India.

The awareness activities organised across various opium cultivation areas also highlighted the significance of 2nd October, the birth anniversary of the Father of the Nation Shri M.K. Gandhi, whose message of self-discipline, social responsibility and a healthy society continues to inspire efforts against substance abuse.

item.content:encoded:
NITI Aayog
Shri Rajiv Gauba calls for a shift to Light-Touch, Risk-Proportionate regulation at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 8:43PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog in his address at the plenary session on “Regulatory Oversight in an Age of Disruption” at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave, highlighted the need for regulatory frameworks to evolve alongside a rapidly changing geopolitical, technological and economic environment. He emphasised that the challenge before policymakers is not to choose between regulation and growth, but to develop regulations that manage risks while supporting innovation, competition and investment.

Setting the context, Shri Gauba observed that geopolitical uncertainty, disruptions to trade routes and global supply chains, and the increasing use of tariffs, export controls and investment restrictions as strategic instruments are reshaping the economic landscape. At the same time, he noted that technological change is advancing faster than many institutions and regulatory frameworks can adapt, particularly in areas such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital technologies.

He also highlighted the growing complexity of modern business models, which increasingly span multiple sectors and technologies. As traditional boundaries between industries become less relevant, he stressed that regulatory frameworks must evolve to address interconnected risks without creating fragmented or conflicting obligations.

Shri Gauba underlined that while regulation is essential for safety, consumer protection, market integrity and systemic stability, excessive or poorly designed regulation can impede innovation, competition and investment. He stressed that national competitiveness depends not only on infrastructure, labour laws and incentives, but also on the clarity, consistency and predictability of the regulatory environment. For businesses considering new investments, he said, the ability to operate at scale and innovate with certainty is an increasingly important consideration.

Emphasising the need for a proportionate approach, Gauba said regulatory requirements should be calibrated to the nature and consequences of the risks involved. He noted that regulators must carefully assess whether new rules are warranted before intervening in new and rapidly evolving sectors and avoid attempting to prescribe solutions for every possible failure.

He further emphasised that regulatory independence must go hand in hand with accountability. While regulators need autonomy to take difficult decisions free from undue influence, public confidence requires transparent decision-making, clear procedures, effective review mechanisms and accountability for regulatory performance.

Gauba also stressed that effective regulation depends on the capacity of the State. As markets and technologies become more sophisticated, regulators need specialised expertise. Strengthening analytical capabilities, attracting specialised talent and developing structured engagement with industry, academia and technology institutions, he said, will be critical to building regulatory capacity.

He called for greater coordination among regulators to address overlapping mandates, avoid duplication and close regulatory gaps as businesses increasingly operate across traditional regulatory domains.

He said that the goal should be a State that is "firm where risks are high, and light-touch where risks are low," but predictable in both cases. Linking this to India's growth trajectory, he said that sustaining the high growth needed for Viksit Bharat by 2047 would require a decisive shift toward light-touch regulation, consistent with Prime Minister Modi’s governance philosophy of Trust Based Governance or Jan Vishwas.

Prime Minister congratulates Indian Men’s Hockey Team on retaining Gold at Asian Games
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 7:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has congratulated the Indian Men’s Hockey Team on retaining the Asian Games Gold with a commanding victory in the final.

Shri Modi said that the team has won back-to-back Asian Games Golds for the first time and secured a fifth Gold overall, describing it as an exceptional campaign by the players.

The Prime Minister said that the triumph is even more special as, for the first time, both India’s Men’s and Women’s Hockey Teams have won Gold at the same Asian Games. He said that Indian Hockey stands tall on the Asian stage.

The Prime Minister’s Office posted on X;

“The 2026 Asian Games have been truly special for Indian Hockey!

Congratulations to our Men’s Hockey Team on retaining the Asian Games Gold with a commanding victory in the final. Back-to-back Asian Games Golds for the first time and a fifth Gold overall…it’s been an exceptional campaign by our players.

This triumph becomes even more special as, for the first time, both our Men’s and Women’s Hockey Teams have won Gold at the same Asian Games. It is clear that Indian Hockey stands tall on the Asian stage: PM @narendramodi”

item.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses Gaupalak Sammelan in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh and inaugurates State-level Exhibition on New Criminal Laws
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Cooperation
item.description: Ministry of Cooperation Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses Gaupalak Sammelan in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh and inaugurates State-level Exhibition on New Criminal Laws In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’, sustained efforts are being made for the prosperity of livestock rearers, farmers and women through cooperation and dairy sector The massive gathering of livestock rearers is an auspicious sign for the White Revolution in Madhya Pradesh Congress ignored the demand for an independent Ministry of Cooperation for 75…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses Gaupalak Sammelan in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh and inaugurates State-level Exhibition on New Criminal Laws
In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’, sustained efforts are being made  for the prosperity of livestock rearers, farmers and women through cooperation and dairy sector
The massive gathering of livestock rearers is an auspicious sign for the White Revolution in Madhya Pradesh
Congress ignored the demand for an independent Ministry of Cooperation for 75 years, while Modi Ji established the Ministry, bringing the greatest benefit to livestock rearers
Mohan Yadav Government has set a target to increase daily milk procurement in Madhya Pradesh from 12 lakh kg to 52 lakh kg
India’s total milk production stood at 14.06 crore tonnes in 2014-15 which has been increased by Modi Ji to 25 crore tonnes in the last 10 years
Per capita milk production has increased by 58%, from 307 grams per day in 2014-15 to 485 grams per day today; India has emerged as the world’s largest milk-producing country
Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra—the top five milk-producing States—are all BJP-ruled; livestock rearers have never benefited in Congress-ruled States
Under White Revolution 2.0, 75,000 new cooperative dairies will be established and 46,000 existing dairies strengthened, with Madhya Pradesh set to derive the maximum benefit
Five technology-driven models for dung processing have been developed, which will help enhance farmers’ income in the coming years
Joining the cooperative system will enable livestock rearers to receive remunerative prices for milk along with benefits from processing and value addition: Shri Amit Shah
In-principle approval for providing 50 acres of land for breed improvement of cattle and buffaloes in Madhya Pradesh; initiative to promote conservation of indigenous breeds and modern breeding technologies
Dairy cooperatives are an important vehicle for women empowerment, rural development, economic prosperity of farmers and the fight against malnutrition:
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, sustained efforts are being made to transform cooperation into an effective instrument for strengthening the rural economy, advancing agricultural development, enhancing the income of livestock rearers and empowering women. As part of these efforts, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the Gaupalak Sammelan at Dussehra Maidan in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, and inaugurated a State-level exhibition on the New Criminal Laws. Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Jagdish Devda and Shri Rajendra Shukla, several Ministers of the State Government, Members of Parliament, MLAs, representatives of the cooperative sector and a large number of livestock rearers and milk producers were present on the occasion.

At the outset of the programme, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation inaugurated the State-level exhibition on the New Criminal Laws and viewed various exhibition sections showcasing the achievements of Madhya Pradesh Police in their implementation.

Addressing the gathering, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the country has made a historic transition from the punishment-centric criminal justice system of the colonial era towards a new system focused on delivering justice to citizens. He said that the fundamental objective of the new laws is not to protect the government but to safeguard the dignity, property and physical security of the citizens of India, and their core principle is ‘justice’, not ‘punishment’. He said that after their full implementation, the new system aims to make the judicial process time-bound, from the registration of an FIR right up to the Supreme Court.

Shri Amit Shah said that modern science and technology have been extensively incorporated into the new criminal justice system. Several modern and scientific provisions, including electronic evidence, online summons, online hearings, video conferencing and forensic science, have been incorporated into the new framework. He said that the new laws also contain specific provisions to deal with crimes relating to the safety of women, missing children, terrorism and mob lynching. He expressed confidence that after their full implementation, India’s criminal justice system will rank among the most modern systems in the world.

Referring to the cooperative sector, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that there had been a long-standing demand in the country for a separate Ministry of Cooperation, and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi infused new energy and momentum into the cooperative sector by establishing an independent Ministry of Cooperation. He said that farmers, livestock rearers and people associated with the rural economy are the biggest beneficiaries of the establishment of this Ministry.

Shri Amit Shah said that livestock rearers selling milk in the open market often do not receive a remunerative price for their produce because of intermediaries, whereas the cooperative system not only enables them to secure better prices but also connects them with the economic benefits generated through milk processing and value addition. He said that robust processing infrastructure is essential for producing value-added products such as ice cream, butter, ghee, cheese and mawa from milk, and the Government is working rapidly in this direction.

Describing breed improvement as an important means of enhancing productivity in the dairy sector, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that he had requested the Madhya Pradesh Government to provide 50 acres of land for programmes related to breed improvement of cattle and buffaloes, and Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav has given in-principle approval for the same. He said that modern breed-improvement technologies will help improve animal health and milk productivity while also promoting the conservation and development of India’s indigenous breeds. The use of modern technologies such as sex-sorted semen will also enhance the prospects of additional economic benefits for livestock rearers.

Referring to the State Government’s target for increasing milk production in Madhya Pradesh, Shri Amit Shah said that it is an ambitious goal and the Central Government will work shoulder to shoulder with the State Government and the livestock rearers of Madhya Pradesh to achieve it.

Highlighting the progress made by India’s dairy sector, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that the country’s total milk production stood at approximately 14.60 crore tonnes in 2014-15 and has now increased to around 24.80 crore tonnes. He said that during the same period, per capita milk availability has increased by approximately 58%, from around 307 grams per day to 485 grams per day. He said that India today is the world’s largest milk-producing country.

Shri Amit Shah said that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and in keeping with the resolve to make India a leading nation in every sphere by 2047, the agriculture, animal husbandry and cooperative sectors are also being modernised and made globally competitive. He said that exports of Indian dairy products have increased to approximately ₹4,666 crore, with Indian dairy products being exported to several countries, including the United Arab Emirates, Bangladesh, the United States, Saudi Arabia and Bhutan.

Referring to White Revolution 2.0, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a target has been set to establish 75,000 new cooperative dairies across the country and strengthen 46,000 existing dairies. He said that a large number of new cooperative dairies will be established in Madhya Pradesh under this initiative, enabling the State’s livestock rearers to benefit from organised markets, better prices, modern processing facilities and a stronger cooperative network.

Shri Amit Shah said that several measures are also being taken to integrate the dairy sector with the Net Zero and circular economy model. Initiatives relating to breed improvement, vaccination, quality livestock, fodder management, artificial insemination and sex-sorted semen are being taken forward. He said that the Sardar Patel Cooperative Dairy Federation Limited has also been established for this purpose.

Highlighting the potential of a dung-based economy, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that various models have been developed to take forward, in an integrated manner, the scientific collection of dung, reduction of methane emissions, clean energy generation, nutrient recycling and creation of rural employment. He said that efforts will be made in the coming years to develop a system under which dung can also become an additional source of income for livestock rearers and farmers in Madhya Pradesh.

Referring to the role of women in dairy cooperatives, Shri Amit Shah said that there can hardly be a more powerful instrument of women empowerment than cooperative dairying. Dairy activities place income directly in the hands of women and thereby link women empowerment with rural development, the economic advancement of farmers and the prosperity of families. He said that the dairy sector is also playing an important role in the country’s fight against malnutrition.

The Union Home Minister referred to the efforts of the Central and State Governments to make Madhya Pradesh free from narcotics and drugs and said that a detailed meeting on the issue is being held with the Chief Minister and the departments concerned. He said that work will be undertaken to formulate and implement a detailed and meticulous action plan to make Madhya Pradesh free from narcotics and drugs, thereby ensuring a safe and bright future for the youth of the State and future generations.

Shri Amit Shah congratulated Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav, the Deputy Chief Ministers and the entire State Government team for the various decisions taken in the interest of livestock rearers. He said that the target of substantially expanding milk production and the cooperative dairy network in Madhya Pradesh is undoubtedly challenging, but the Central Government will extend its full support to the State Government and livestock rearers in achieving this objective. The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that the Central and State Governments are working with the resolve to take the cooperative and dairy sectors to new heights so that Madhya Pradesh prospers through dairy development and cattle rearing, its farmers prosper and, above all, women prosper.

On the occasion, a Memorandum of Understanding was also exchanged between KRIBHCO and the Madhya Pradesh State Biodiversity Board for developing an urban forest in Bhopal under the ‘Morvan Project’.

During the programme, Shri Amit Shah digitally laid the foundation stone for a 3 lakh litres per day milk processing plant in Ujjain, to be established at a cost of ₹255 crore. A 40,000 litres per day Product Dairy Plant, constructed in Bhopal at a cost of approximately ₹16.5 crore, and a state-of-the-art State-level Central Laboratory, built at a cost of ₹12.42 crore, were also inaugurated. The strengthening works of the Mini Dairy Plant in Shivpuri, undertaken at a cost of ₹6.5 crore, were also inaugurated digitally. These projects will further strengthen milk processing capacity, quality testing facilities and dairy-sector infrastructure in Madhya Pradesh.

During the programme, bonuses were provided to livestock rearers associated with the Bhopal and Indore Milk Unions, while financial assistance was extended to Gaushalas through a single click. Dividends were distributed to members of dairy cooperative societies and livestock rearers were felicitated. Recognising the important role of women livestock rearers, ‘Gaupalak Didis’ were also honoured. In addition, sanction letters were presented under the Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Kamdhenu Yojana.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Ministry of Education Approves Five Centres of Excellence for Studies in Classical Languages
Centres to advance research, preservation, digitisation and wider dissemination of India’s linguistic and literary heritage
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India, has approved the establishment of five Centres of Excellence (CoEs) for studies in Classical Assamese, Classical Bengali, Classical Marathi, Classical Pali and Classical Prakrit.

The initiative will provide dedicated institutional support for advanced academic research, preservation and digitisation of linguistic and literary heritage, and wider dissemination of knowledge relating to these Classical Languages.

The Centres of Excellence will be established at the following Higher Educational Institutions:

S. No.

Classical Language

Centre of Excellence

1.

Classical Assamese

Tezpur University, Assam

2.

Classical Bengali

Visva-Bharati University, West Bengal

3.

Classical Marathi

Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (Deemed to be University), Pune, Maharashtra

4.

Classical Pali

Central University of Odisha, Odisha

5.

Classical Prakrit

Central University of Gujarat, Gujarat

The establishment of these five Centres marks a significant step towards strengthening the institutional ecosystem for the study, research and preservation of India’s Classical Languages.

Key areas of focus

The Centres of Excellence will focus on four broad areas:

Strengthening academic research and scholarship:
The Centres will provide dedicated institutional platforms for advanced research, scholarly work and academic engagement in the respective Classical Languages.

Preservation and digitisation: The Centres will support the documentation, preservation and digitisation of linguistic and literary resources, contributing to the long-term conservation of India’s rich textual heritage.

Wider dissemination of Classical Language heritage: The Centres will facilitate wider access to and dissemination of linguistic, literary and knowledge traditions associated with the respective Classical Languages.

Strengthening regional academic ecosystems:
Located across five States—Assam, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Odisha and Gujarat, the Centres will strengthen regional ecosystems for higher education, research and scholarship in Classical Languages.

The initiative reinforces the Government’s efforts to preserve and promote India’s rich linguistic and literary heritage while strengthening institutions of higher education as centres of research and scholarship.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVAL SHIPS SAHYADRI AND KULISH CONCLUDE PARTICIPATION IN AIME 2026
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 5:26PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ships Sahyadri and Kulish concluded their participation in the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise (AIME 2026), conducted in the Philippines under the theme ‘Anchored in Trust, United at Sea’. The exercise provided opportunities for professional interaction, operational coordination and maritime training through the Harbour and Sea Phases.

The Opening Ceremony was followed by the Harbour Phase, comprising a range of engagements including, Key Leaders’ Engagements, sporting events, Yoga, Community Interaction and Subject Matter Expert Exchanges. A Table-Top Exercise, Operational Synchronisation and Pre-Sail Brief facilitated coordination and preparation for the Sea Phase.

During the Sea Phase, INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish participated in coordinated maritime exercises including Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief, Visit-Board-Search-Seizure (VBSS) and Underway Replenishment drills. Helicopter exercises included cross-deck landings, vertical replenishment and CASEVAC drills. These activities enhanced coordination and interoperability among the participating maritime forces.

The Harbour and Sea Phases of AIME 2026 reinforced trust and enhanced interoperability, contributing to effective maritime partnerships. The participation of INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish reaffirmed the Indian Navy’s continued commitment to engagement with partner maritime forces, in consonance with India’s Act East Policy and the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

Five items are sports-related, while others celebrate the state’s religious and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Haryana’s Sporting Achievements Take Centre Stage in 8th Edition of PM Mementos Auction
Seven mementos from Haryana include items presented by three Paralympic gold medallists, alongside objects reflecting the state’s religious and cultural heritage
Auction proceeds will go to the Namami Gange Project
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi

This edition features seven mementos from Haryana, with sporting achievements forming a prominent part of the collection. Five items are sports-related, while others celebrate the state’s religious and cultural heritage.

Open for public bidding, these mementos carry stories of achievement and perseverance. The proceeds from the auction will go to the Namami Gange Project.

Celebrating Haryana’s Paralympic Champions

 

 

Among the featured items is an arrow presented by Harwinder Singh, who became the first Indian to win a Paralympic gold medal in archery. Two mementos are associated with Navdeep Singh, who won gold in the men’s F41 javelin throw event at the Paris 2024 Paralympics. His cap and signed shirt offer members of the public an opportunity to own keepsakes connected to this sporting achievement.

The collection also features an authentic Yonex badminton racket and India team shirt presented by Paralympic badminton gold medallist Nitesh Kumar. Together, these items represent Haryana’s contribution to India’s sporting achievements.

Haryana’s Religious and Cultural Heritage

 

Alongside the sporting memorabilia, the collection includes a metal statue of Goddess Sheetala Devi. Crafted from high quality metal, the statue features intricate detailing, with a lustrous finish that enhances its divine presence.

A souvenir commemorating the Gita Updesh Sthali of Dharmakshetra Kurukshetra reflecting Haryana’s association with the Bhagavad Gita also adorns the collection.

These seven mementos in the 8th edition of PM Mementos, bring together different facets of Haryana. The auction gives these gifts a larger public purpose, with the proceeds supporting the Namami Gange Project.

For auction dates, participation details and the complete catalogue, visit the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: pmmementos.gov.in

item.title: As part of Special Gram Sabha on Gandhi Jayanti, Jal Arpan Observed in more than 1850 Gram Panchayats Across Rural India to Strengthen Community Ownership of Rural Water Supply Systems Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Jal Shakti
item.description: Ministry of Jal Shakti As part of Special Gram Sabha on Gandhi Jayanti, Jal Arpan Observed in more than 1850 Gram Panchayats Across Rural India to Strengthen Community Ownership of Rural Water Supply Systems Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 In A First, Har Ghar Jal Certificates Generated in Regional Languages issued to Gram Panchayats Through Jal Arpan module Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti and Special Gram Sabhas held across States/UTs, more than 1,850 Gram Panchayats/villages observed Jal Arpan- a key reform under Jal Jeevan…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
As part of Special Gram Sabha on Gandhi Jayanti, Jal Arpan Observed in more than 1850 Gram Panchayats Across Rural India to Strengthen Community Ownership of Rural Water Supply Systems Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
In A First, Har Ghar Jal Certificates Generated in Regional Languages issued to Gram Panchayats Through Jal Arpan module
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi

On the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti and Special Gram Sabhas held across States/UTs, more than 1,850 Gram Panchayats/villages observed Jal Arpan- a key reform under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0- that places rural drinking water systems in the hands of the communities. This marked the formal handover of completed rural water supply schemes to Gram Panchayats and Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), reflecting the Mission's shift towards community-led management and sustainable delivery of drinking water services.

In a first, the Jal Arpan module also enabled generation of Har Ghar Jal Certificates in regional languages for eligible Gram Panchayats and villages. 346 Har Ghar Jal Certificates were generated for eligible Gram Panchayats and villages and issued in regional languages, making the certification process more accessible and citizen-centric while further strengthening community ownership of drinking water services. The Jal Arpan Module, now has provision of Har Gahr Jal certificate generations in Hindi, English and 17 other regional languages including Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Gujarati, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu, enabling communities to access programme information and certification in their own languages

Jal Arpan celebrations witnessed active participation of Gram Panchayats, Village Water & Sanitation Committees, frontline functionaries, women volunteers and community members across rural India. Completed rural water supply schemes, successfully commissioned following the prescribed trial run period, were formally handed over to Gram Panchayats and VWSCs for operation, maintenance and long-term sustainability. Activities such as Jal Sankalp, Jal Bandhan, demonstrations on water quality testing using Field Test Kits (FTKs), awareness programmes and recognition of community contributors were organised in several villages. The States and UTs also undertook activities related to water quality surveillance and monitoring, post monsoon water quality testing of sources to ensure the safety and reliability of drinking water services. Community-led water quality monitoring is being strengthened through the active involvement of women.

Digital governance and asset management are being strengthened under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 through Sujalam Bharat where water supply assets and piped water supply sources are being geotagged. On the same occasion, 2691 water supply assets including around 700 sources were geo-tagged across the country. These efforts are supporting improved planning, monitoring and long-term sustainability of rural water supply systems while creating a comprehensive digital inventory of drinking water assets.

In the country’s journey towards water-resilience, as on date, more than 15.96 crore rural households, representing over 82% of rural households in the country, have drinking water tap connections under the Jal Jeevan Mission. To bring transparency, accountability and real-time monitoring to the process, the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation has developed a dedicated Jal Arpan digital module under Jal Jeevan Mission. The module provides a structured digital record of scheme handover and supports Gram Panchayat-led management of rural drinking water systems. The Government of India remains committed to working in partnership with States, Union Territories, Gram Panchayats and local communities to ensure that every rural household continues to receive safe, adequate and reliable drinking water services.

The observance of Jal Arpan resonates with Mahatma Gandhi’s vision of community participation, local self-governance and collective responsibility, with Gram Panchayats and village communities playing a central role in sustaining drinking water services and ensuring long-term water security.

item.title: India’s First 5.56 km Free‑Space Quantum Key Distribution Link Demonstrated
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Electronics & IT
item.description: Ministry of Electronics & IT India’s First 5.56 km Free‑Space Quantum Key Distribution Link Demonstrated Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi QNu Labs, in collaboration with Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo‑informatics (BISAG‑N) and IIT Gandhinagar, has successfully demonstrated India’s first free‑space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link at a scale of 5.56 km. The field trial, conducted on the night of September 27–28, established a secure quantum communication channel between BISAG‑N and IIT Gandhinagar. Using QNu Labs’…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
India’s First 5.56 km Free‑Space Quantum Key Distribution Link Demonstrated
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi

QNu Labs, in collaboration with Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo‑informatics (BISAG‑N) and IIT Gandhinagar, has successfully demonstrated India’s first free‑space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link at a scale of 5.56 km.

The field trial, conducted on the night of September 27–28, established a secure quantum communication channel between BISAG‑N and IIT Gandhinagar. Using QNu Labs’ Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking system, the trial achieved a stable Quantum Bit Error Rate below 5% and generated secure keys at a rate of 230–260 bps. These keys were integrated with BISAG‑N’s post‑quantum cryptography enabled Vedic Kavach platform, enabling successful end‑to‑end encryption and decryption of test messages.

The demonstration combined two complementary layers of quantum security: QNu Labs’ hardware‑based QKD device Armos over free‑space optical channels and BISAG‑N’s Vedic Kavach software‑based post‑quantum cryptography with quantum random number generation. This integrated architecture ensures resilience even if the physical quantum channel is temporarily unavailable.

Dr. Vinay Thakur, Director General, BISAG‑N, stated that the integration of Vedic Kavach with QNu Labs’ QKD technology marks a significant step towards practical quantum‑resilient communication systems.

Sunil Gupta, Co‑founder and CEO, QNu Labs, emphasized that the successful 5.56 km demonstration paves the way for longer‑distance quantum‑secure networks and satellite‑based quantum communication.

Cmde Manish Tripathi (Retd.), In‑charge, ISTF, IIT Gandhinagar, added that the demonstration provides a valuable field environment for advancing practical quantum communication technologies and showcases how academia, indigenous technology and real‑world experimentation can be integrated to meet emerging secure communication requirements.

The trial provides a foundation for advancing India’s capabilities in secure communication infrastructure, strengthening resilience against emerging quantum‑era security threats.

About BISAG‑N: An autonomous scientific society under MeitY, BISAG‑N works in space technology applications, satellite communication, geo‑informatics and supports technology‑driven governance.

About IIT Gandhinagar: Founded in 2008, the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) is a leading institution focused on excellence in engineering, science, technology, humanities and social sciences. The Institute promotes interdisciplinary research, innovative education and solutions to real-world challenges.

About QNu Labs: Founded in 2016, QNu Labs is India’s pioneer in quantum‑secure digital infrastructure, offering sovereign products and solutions deployed globally.

****

Vinod Kumar / Dhanya Ranjan / Kanishk Sharma

item.title: In culmination of 10 years of dedicated efforts, Union Environment Minister and CM (Rajasthan) initiate the process for release of captive-bred Great Indian Bustards into the Wild at Desert National Park, Jaislamer
item.category: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
item.description: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change In culmination of 10 years of dedicated efforts, Union Environment Minister and CM (Rajasthan) initiate the process for release of captive-bred Great Indian Bustards into the Wild at Desert National Park, Jaislamer A critical step in GIB Recovery Programme - to aid progressive Refining of Protocols for Reintroduction of Captive-bred Birds into their Natural Habitat Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi In a significant milestone for the conservation of the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard (GIB), during…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
In culmination of 10 years of dedicated efforts, Union Environment Minister and CM (Rajasthan) initiate the process for release of captive-bred Great Indian Bustards into the Wild at Desert National Park, Jaislamer
A critical step in GIB Recovery Programme - to aid progressive Refining of Protocols for Reintroduction of Captive-bred Birds into their Natural Habitat
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant milestone for the conservation of the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard (GIB), during the Wildlife Week 2026 Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, and Chief Minister (Rajasthan), Shri Bhajan Lal Sharma (through VC), today participated in the initiation of the process for release of two captive-bred Great Indian Bustards from the soft-release facility into the wild to be undertaken tomorrow at the Desert National Park, Jaisalmer. This rewilding of the GIB is the fruit of continuous hard work, dedication and scientific pursuit over a decade in building a viable population of the State bird of Rajasthan. The dignitaries also reviewed the progress of GIB Conservation Breeding Centre at Ramdevra and Sam and inaugurated the newly developed Rewilding Aviary, while also releasing the brochure on the decadal journey of GIB in the landscape. Rajasthan State Minister for Forest and Environment, Shri Sanjay Sharma, along with senior officers of the Union and State Governments attended the event.

The project has seen a remarkable beginning in Rajasthan and subsequently a successful ‘jumpstart’ initiative in Gujarat. The Union Minister recently reviewed the soft release and conservation facility at Naliya, Kutch in Gujrat. Tomorrow's release would mark an important transition in India’s GIB conservation programme from establishing a viable conservation-breeding population towards rewilding and augmentation of the species in its natural habitat. The exercise was undertaken in a carefully controlled manner with limited presence at the release site to minimise human-induced disturbance to the birds. Learnings from the pilot release will be used to progressively refine the protocols for subsequent releases.

In his address during the evening, the Chief Minister of Rajasthan called this day of rewilding of the State Bird as a day of pride for the whole State. He highlighted how under the coordinated efforts of the Union and State Governments, the GIB which is part of the Thar's cultural heritage has been brought back from the brink of extinction. The Chief Minister also detailed the funding support provided by the State Government for the GIB Conservation Programme, besides other successful interventions in the field of environmental conservation across the State.

Addressing the inaugural session, Shri Bhupender Yadav highlighted that the whole region of Thar Desert has emotional and cultural connect with GIB. The Union Minister thanked Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision that led to the success of the conservation programme for GIB, which has become a global example during the last decade. He commended the efforts of the officials of Union Environment Ministry, State forest department, scientists of WII and local communities to have achieved the swift progress under the GIB Conservation Programme that has today reached the stage of rewilding the bird.

Shri Yadav stated that the success of this programme would also get economic benefits for local communities in the form of eco-tourism, besides GIB conservation's ecological benefits as the umbrella species of the Thar ecosystem. The Minister further highlighted the importance of GIB in grassland conservation, land degradation neutrality and working as an important stopover for migratory birds in central Asian flyways.

During the visit, while reviewing the incubation and breeding facilities Shri Yadav interacted with officials and scientists associated with the conservation programme. The Rewilding Aviary at Ramdevra, measuring 160 m × 64 m × 14 m, has been constructed by the Rajasthan Forest Department through the Rajasthan State Road Development and Construction Corporation Ltd. (RSRDC), with a sanctioned budget of ₹9.25 crore from the Government of Rajasthan in consultation of experts and scientists of Ministry and WII. The large, pillar-less facility provides unobstructed flight space for captive-bred GIBs to develop flight muscles, adapt to natural conditions and exhibit natural behaviour in preparation for their eventual release.

The Bustard Recovery Programme

It is a collaborative initiative of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Rajasthan Forest Department and Wildlife Institute of India (WII), with technical collaboration from the International Fund for Houbara Conservation and funding support from National CAMPA. The ongoing National Action Plan envisages conservation breeding, scientifically informed habitat management, threat mitigation, habitat restoration and community engagement.

The conservation-breeding programme has achieved significant progress. The GIB facilities at Sam and Ramdevra presently house 97 birds, of which 40 originated from wild-laid eggs and 57 have been bred in captivity. Of these, 86 birds are being maintained for captive reproduction, while 11 have been earmarked for release into the wild. Captive reproduction resulted in 24 live chicks during 2025 and 29 during 2026. Scientific interventions under the programme such as the novel ‘jumpstart’ approach are aiding in the species’ recovery, wherein six chicks in Rajasthan and two chicks in Gujarat have been hatched by placing captive-laid eggs in wild nests that were accepted by the incubating females.

These interventions – enabled by successful conservation breeding of GIB – are being reinforced with significant efforts in restoring habitats by Rajasthan Forest Department that includes the establishment of ~200 sqkm of fenced grassland enclosures inside the Desert National Park, which serve as the prime breeding habitats for the species, according to long-term telemetry studies of WII. The species’ conservation actions are being guided by the Judgement of the Supreme Court of India, based on recommendations of the Expert Committee constituted for this purpose.

The release of captive-bred GIBs represents the next critical step in the species recovery programme and will provide important scientific learnings for progressively developing and refining protocols for reintroduction of captive-bred birds into their natural habitat. As a prelude to Shri Yadav's visit to GIB conservation facilities at Jaisalmer, public awareness and outreach activities were organized across Rajasthan.

*****

Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
DARE/ICAR Launches Special Campaign 6.0 with Nationwide Cleanliness Drives and Felicitation of Safai Mitras
Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan felicitates Safai Mitras at ICAR-CCARI in Goa
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 2:39PM by PIB Delhi

Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) commenced Special Campaign 6.0 on 2nd October, 2026 with extensive cleanliness and sanitation activities across ICAR institutes and establishments located throughout the country. Marking the commencement of the campaign, officials of ICAR Headquarters actively participated in cleanliness drives at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), Pusa, New Delhi. The campaign underscores the collective commitment of DARE and ICAR towards promoting clean and hygienic workplaces, encouraging public participation and fostering a sustained culture of cleanliness in line with the spirit of Swachhata.

As part of Special Campaign 6.0, DARE and ICAR institutes and establishments across the country undertook a range of cleanliness and sanitation activities, including cleanliness drives and Shramdaan in institutional premises, villages, roads, pathways and other identified areas. Special Gram Sabhas, Swachhata Sabhas and awareness programmes were organised to promote cleanliness, sanitation, hygiene, waste management and community responsibility. Plogging activities were conducted for the collection and removal of litter and unwanted material from public and institutional spaces, while cleaned areas were further improved through plantation and greening initiatives, including activities under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” campaign. Dustbins were distributed and placed at identified locations to encourage responsible waste disposal and community participation. SafaiMitras, sanitation workers and volunteers were recognised and appreciated for their contribution towards sustaining cleanliness. The campaign also focused on the beautification and transformation of cleaned spaces, supported by before-and-after photographic documentation, while promoting sustainable practices such as vermicomposting of water hyacinth and systematic weeding and review of old files for appropriate disposal and record management. These initiatives resulted in enhanced community participation and collective ownership of cleanliness, improved cleanliness of institutional and public spaces, greater awareness of responsible waste disposal, integration of cleanliness with environmental sustainability through plantation and greening, and wider recognition of the contribution of SafaiMitras, sanitation workers and volunteers. The campaign also encouraged practical environmental and resource-management practices, including vermicomposting and systematic management of old records.

In ICAR–Central Coastal Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR–CCARI), Goa, highlight of the occasion was the Shramik Samman, wherein Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Ji, felicitated Safai Mitras of ICAR–CCARI with shawls, bouquets and gifts, as a mark of appreciation for the dedicated services of all Safai Mitras who work throughout the year to maintain a clean and hygienic campus. Chief Minister of Goa, Dr.Pramod Sawant, appreciated the participation and efforts of ICAR–CCARI under Swachhata Hi Seva–2026. Union Minister of State Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Rajya Sabha Member Shri Sadanand Shet Tanawade also graced the occasion. The programme highlighted the spirit of Swachhata, Seva and Shramik Samman, recognising the invaluable contribution of Safai Mitras towards a cleaner and healthier environment.

The ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR-IARI), New Delhi, observed Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2nd October 2026 under the theme “Swachhta Mein Sahbhag – Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”, with a series of cleanliness activities across the Institute and a call for sustained participation towards maintaining a clean and healthy institutional environment. A floral tribute was also paid to Mahatma Gandhi on the occasion of his birth anniversary.

In his address, Secretary (DARE) & DG (ICAR), Dr. Mangi Lal Jat, appreciated the cleanliness drive undertaken by ICAR-IARI and called for making Swachhata a year-round activity, with cleanliness programmes being undertaken in a team-based manner. He emphasised that cleanliness and a better workplace environment contribute to the overall well-being of employees and support the advancement of science and the health of people. Dr. Mangi Lal Jat also highlighted the importance of team building and creating a positive workplace environment, noting its relevance to both institutional functioning and mental well-being. He stressed the need for second-line leadership development, including handholding and mentoring future science leaders. He further emphasised the importance of nurturing students for their holistic development, enabling them to grow as responsible professionals and future contributors to science and society. Emphasising accountability in institutional functioning, he noted that every individual should remain responsible for their assigned work and contribute sincerely to the responsibilities entrusted to them.

As part of the programme, prizes were distributed to the winners of the painting competition organised by the Post Graduate School Students’ Union, ICAR-IARI, during the Swachhata Abhiyaan. The competition provided students an opportunity to express their ideas on cleanliness and environmental responsibility through art.

 

At ICAR-NAARM, Hyderabad, as part of the Swachhta Special Campaign 6.0, a tribute to Mahatma Gandhi and felicitation of Safai Mitras were organized. The programme commenced with a tribute to Mahatma Gandhi on the occasion of Swachh Bharat Diwas.

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign, Swachh Bharat Diwas was celebrated at ICAR–CAFRI, Jhansi. The programme focused on promoting cleanliness, sanitation, community participation and responsible waste management. The activity highlighted the importance of collective action and Shramdaan in maintaining clean surroundings. The contribution of Safai Mitras and sanitation workers was also acknowledged, emphasising their important role in maintaining hygiene and sanitation. Participants were encouraged to adopt cleanliness as a regular practice and contribute towards maintaining clean and healthy surroundings. The programme concluded with a renewed commitment to Swachhata, sustainable practices and collective responsibility.

 

As part of the “Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign 2026” Encouraging staff and citizens to contribute one hour of voluntary Swachhata service (Shramdan) through a cleanliness drive & plant trees at the cleaned CTUs to nature urban green under Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam was organized on 02.10.2026 behind the ATIC building and near the old Type III & IV quarters of ICAR-Central Island Agricultural Research Institute, Sri Vijaya Puram. The planting material of West Indian Cherry around 55 planted by the staff members and cleaned the area as well. A total of 85 staff members actively participated the program.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Union Minister of Jal Shakti Leads Special Gram Sabha Observance on Swachh Bharat Diwas 2026
Senior DDWS officials participated in Special Gram Sabhas across States/UTs
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 2:32PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister Shri C. R. Patil participated in Special Gram Sabha at Majigam village in Chikhli Block, Navsari District, Gujarat on Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 October 2026. The Special Gram Sabha was also attended by Shri Naresh Patel, Cabinet Minister, Government of Gujarat, Joint Secretary & Mission Director, Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), Ms. Aishvarya Singh, District Collector and District Development Officer along with senior officials from State and District administration.

During the Special Gram Sabha, Union Minister felicitated sanitation workers and called upon everyone to make cleanliness a collective commitment and not merely a one-day campaign, but an integral part of our daily lives, behaviour and collective responsibility. He emphasized that we must resolve that neither will we litter, nor will we allow others to do so the same.

During his address, the Union Minister recalled the emphasis placed by Mahatma Gandhi on ‘Swachhata’ alongside ‘Swatantrata’ and mentioned how post-Independence the most significant efforts for Swachhta have been undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Under this, a nationwide Jan Andolan in the form of Swachh Bharat Mission has transformed rural sanitation scenario. This Janbhagidari for Swachh Bharat continues to drive the mission at grassroots level.

Along with other topics, discussions during the Special Gram Sabha also focused on achievements of SHS 2026, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and Swachh Seva Aankalan, the GP level annual digital self-assessment framework on which a presentation was made by JS&MD.

The Union Minister had earlier visited the “Waste to Art” exhibit of the GP that highlighted creative reuse of discarded materials, encouraging responsible waste management practices within the community.

A plantation drive was conducted under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’, during which Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Patil, and JS & MD, SBM(G), planted trees. All dignitaries and Gram Sabha participants together took the Swachhta pledge.

On Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 October 2026, Special Gram Sabhas were organized across rural India as a key activity under Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026. These Gram Sabhas provided a platform for Gram Panchayats and rural communities to review local sanitation and waste management efforts; discuss the outcomes of SHS 2026; review the status of four-way source segregation in line with the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026; identify and register bulk waste generators; and undertake discussions on Swachh Seva Aankalan in ODF Plus (Model) Gram Panchayats.

The Special Gram Sabha provided an opportunity and platform to undertake gap assessment and integrate relevant actions into Panchayat Development Plans, particularly GPDPs, for coordinated implementation at the grassroots.

Senior DDWS officials join Special Gram Sabhas and sanitation activities across States/UTs

  • In Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Deputy Secretary, DDWS participated in the Special Gram Sabha at Sayli Gram Panchayat, which included discussions on Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and SWM Rules, 2026, the Swachhata Shapath and felicitation of sanitation workers. The visit also included visit to an STP, and a plantation drive under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’.
  • In Jharkhand, Deputy Secretary, DDWS, participated in the Special Gram Sabha held at Pindarkom village, Sithiyo Gram Panchayat, Namkum Block, Ranchi District. The Gram Sabha included discussions on the draft of Swachh Seva Aankalan and the process of addressing identified gaps, felicitation of sanitation workers, Swachhata Shapath, plantation under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ and inspection of sanitation assets.
  • In Haryana, Deputy Secretary, DDWS, participated in the Special Gram Sabha held at Ratipur village in Palwal Block, Palwal District. The visit included a plantation drive, an inspection of the Segregation shed and interactions with the community on Swachh Seva Aankalan, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and local sanitation efforts.
  • In Madhya Pradesh, Assistant Adviser, DDWS attended the Special Gram Sabhas held at Mugaliya Haat and Jhirniya Gram Panchayats in Phanda Block, Bhopal District. During the Gram Sabhas, participants took the Swachhata Shapath and discussed Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and Swachh Seva Aankalan. The visit also included a plantation drive and an inspection visit to a segregation shed.

item.content:encoded:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
Shri Harivansh Leads Indian Parliamentary Delegation to 153rd IPU Assembly in Tanzania
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 12:56PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, 3 October 2026: The Indian Parliamentary Delegation, led by the Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh, has departed for Arusha, United Republic of Tanzania, to participate in the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) and related meetings being held from 5 to 9 October 2026.

 The IPU Assembly will bring together parliamentarians from across the world for discussions on the theme “Enhancing good governance and empowering communities through inclusivity, trust and opportunities for all.”

The Indian delegation comprises Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha (Leader of the Delegation); Shri Anurag Singh Thakur, MP, Lok Sabha; Smt. Aparajita Sarangi, MP, Lok Sabha; Dr. Sasmit Patra, MP, Rajya Sabha; Dr. Sanjay Jaiswal, MP, Lok Sabha; Smt. Kamaljeet Sehrawat, MP, Lok Sabha; Dr. Lata Wankhede, MP, Lok Sabha; Smt. Bijuli Kalita Medhi, MP, Lok Sabha; and Shri N. K. Premachandran, MP, Lok Sabha.

The delegation will participate in a wide range of meetings, panel discussions and workshops on issues of contemporary global relevance, and articulate India's perspectives on these matters.

Shri Harivansh will participate in the Governing Council, the General Debate, the debate on the emergency item and the hearing with candidates for the position of IPU President.

Members of the Indian delegation will participate in discussions on democracy and human rights, peace and international security, sustainable development, women’s participation, science and technology, counter-terrorism, health, mental health, critical minerals, artificial intelligence and the future of work, maritime security, climate change and protection of mountain and ocean ecosystems, among other subjects. 

The participation of the Indian Parliamentary Delegation reflects India's continued engagement with the IPU and its commitment to parliamentary diplomacy, multilateral dialogue and cooperation among parliaments on issues affecting global peace, development, democracy and the empowerment of communities.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah congratulates all the agencies for achieving a historic milestone by securing the deportation of hardened narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Türkiye
Obtaining Turkish citizenship under the fake identity of Navab Virk, he had continued to smuggle heroin and methamphetamine to India from Afghanistan
Today he has been brought back to India and put behind bars in connection with cases involving drug trafficking and other crimes he is accused of
Modi govt is committed to destroying every narco-cartel before Dec 2029
Modi government has succeeded in bringing back a total of 288 fugitives from 36 countries since 2019 to August, 2026
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 12:18PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah congratulates all the agencies for achieving a historic milestone by securing the deportation of hardened narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Türkiye.

In his post on X platform, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said “Modi govt has achieved a historic milestone by securing the deportation of hardened narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Türkiye. Obtaining Turkish citizenship under the fake identity of Navab Virk, he had continued to smuggle heroin and methamphetamine to India from Afghanistan. Our agencies tracked him down, ripping apart veil after veil to unmask his true identity, and secured his deportation. Today he has been brought back to India and put behind bars in connection with cases involving drug trafficking and other crimes he is accused of. Congratulations to all the agencies for this success. Modi govt is committed to destroying every narco-cartel before Dec 2029.”

Modi government has launched a coordinated campaign to bring back fugitives. Since 2019 to August, 2026, a total of 288 fugitives from 36 countries have bene brought back to India.

Previous governments lacked the political will to bring back fugitives; Modi government has made the extradition of fugitives a 'national priority'. In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah has emphasized a three-pronged strategy against fugitives: global outreach, strong coordination, and smart diplomacy. Shri Amit Shah has described the issue of fugitive offenders as one that is intrinsically linked to the country's sovereignty, economic stability, law and order, and national security.

The Modi Government enacted the NIA (Amendment) Act and the UAPA (Amendment) Act in 2019, and from 2020 onwards, the process of bringing fugitive offenders back to India was taken up in a mission mode. As a result, enforcement efforts were no longer confined to proscribed organizations alone. The scope of action was expanded to include individual terrorists, handlers, funding networks, and support systems based abroad, significantly strengthening India's ability to pursue fugitives and dismantle their networks.

To strengthen coordination, connectivity, and information-sharing between India and global law enforcement agencies, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah launched BHARATPOL in January 2025. BHARATPOL has created a comprehensive information infrastructure by integrating the CBI, State Police Headquarters (through Interpol Liaison Officers - ILOs), and District Police Headquarters onto a single platform. Under this initiative, more than 1,400 units of State and Central agencies have been connected through the portal, ensuring seamless flow of information. As a result, the response time for information-sharing between the CBI and other law enforcement agencies has been significantly reduced. Today, information sought by the CBI is generally shared by other law enforcement agencies within 10 to 20 days, and in some cases, within 3 to 10 days, substantially improving the efficiency of investigations and extradition proceedings.

The Modi Government has enforced the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) with greater rigor. Through stringent enforcement of PMLA, Modi Government attached assets worth ₹17,874 crore belonging to fugitive criminals between 2019 and 2026.

Over the past three years, Red Corner Notices have been issued against 401 fugitive criminals. 182 Red Corner notices have been issued till July, 2026.

Modi govt has achieved a historic milestone by securing the deportation of hardened narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Türkiye.

Obtaining Turkish citizenship under the fake identity of Navab Virk, he had continued to smuggle heroin and methamphetamine to India from…

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Delivers Inaugural Address at 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi
“Economic Resilience Cannot Be Separated from Social Resilience”: Vice-President
“Inclusion is the Foundation of Resilience in an Age of Flux”: Vice-President
“True Resilience Lies in Ensuring No Citizen, Enterprise or Region is Left Behind”: Vice-President
“India Has Demonstrated That Democracy and Development Can Advance Together”: Vice-President
Posted On: 03 OCT 2026 11:56AM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today delivered the inaugural address at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, organised on the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux.” Addressing policymakers, economists, academics, business leaders and other distinguished participants, he highlighted the need for resilient, inclusive and responsive economic policies amid rapid global changes.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan delivered the inaugural address at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, organised on the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux.”

He emphasised that economic resilience cannot be separated from social resilience, and that… pic.twitter.com/KWuGXK1apZ

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 3, 2026

Referring to the legacy of the Institute of Economic Growth (IEG), the Vice-President said the Institute has remained closely connected with India’s development journey since its establishment in 1952 under Professor V. K. R. V. Rao. He emphasised that sound policymaking must be grounded in an understanding of ground realities, with policies remaining flexible and responsive to changing circumstances.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that in times of flux, decisiveness must be embedded in consensus. Debate and discussion are integral to democracy, he said, but must ultimately lead to decisions that command broad acceptance. As Chairman of Rajya Sabha, he noted that free and transparent debate strengthens democracy, while rights and duties must go hand in hand.

The Vice-President said India has demonstrated that democracy and development can advance together. India’s economic growth and inclusive progress have been achieved within a democratic framework, while consensus-building has given economic reforms greater durability and sustainability. He said this experience provides an important foundation for the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Emphasising that economic resilience cannot be separated from social resilience, the Vice-President highlighted the transformative role of the JAM trinity, Direct Benefit Transfer and GST in strengthening financial inclusion, transparency and formalisation. He noted that more than 590 million Jan Dhan accounts had been opened as of August 2026, while GST registrations had risen from around 6.65 million in 2017 to 16.5 million in May 2026.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said inclusion must go beyond bringing people into the formal economy and must enable people to create value, generate income and become entrepreneurs. He highlighted the contribution of around 9.2 million Self-Help Groups covering more than 100 million rural women, and the emergence of over 34.6 million Lakhpati Didis. He said the growing participation of women in education and the economy reflects India’s transition from women’s empowerment to women-led development.

The Vice-President emphasised that resilience is built not merely in boardrooms and financial markets, but also when a woman in a village has a bank account, receives benefits directly, enters the formal economy and transforms a Self-Help Group into an enterprise. He said that more than 250 million Indians have moved out of extreme poverty, describing it as a historic achievement, and stressed that every State, district and village must be an equal partner in India’s development journey.

Calling for stronger research and institutional partnerships, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan welcomed collaborations among the University of Delhi, Delhi School of Economics, London School of Economics and the Institute of Economic Growth. He said such partnerships, along with India’s expanding trade engagements, can strengthen research, education, innovation and entrepreneurship.

Concluding, the Vice-President said that India’s resilience will come “not from resisting change, but from embracing it with confidence, inclusion and a spirit of collective endeavour.” He expressed confidence that the deliberations at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave would contribute meaningfully to the national endeavour of building a developed India by 2047.

IEG President, Board of Trustees, Shri N. K. Singh; Chairman, Board of Governors, IEG, Dr. Michael Debabrata Patra; and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to address Gopalak Sammelan in Bhopal and inaugurate State-Level Exhibition on Nyaya Sanhita
Shri Amit Shah to digitally lay foundation stone for a 3 lakh litres per day capacity Milk Processing Plant in Ujjain at a cost of ₹255 crore
Product Dairy Plant with a capacity of 40,000 litres per day, built at a cost of ₹16.5 crore, and a state-of-the-art State-Level Central Laboratory worth ₹12.42 crore to be inaugurated in Bhopal
Strengthening works of Mini Dairy Plant in Shivpuri, undertaken at a cost of ₹6.5 crore, to also be digitally inaugurated
Bonus to be distributed to members of Bhopal and Indore Milk Unions through a single click; financial assistance to also be provided to Gaushalas
₹15.10 crore dividend to be distributed among members of Dairy Cooperative Societies; Gopalak Didis to also be felicitated
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 10:18PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, several significant initiatives are being undertaken to make the country’s cooperative sector stronger, modern and self-reliant. Special emphasis is being laid on making cooperative institutions an effective vehicle for strengthening the rural economy and enhancing farmers’ prosperity, while leveraging dairy cooperatives to augment the income and economic participation of livestock rearers, milk producers and, in particular, women members. In furtherance of these efforts, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will participate as the Chief Guest at the Gopalak Sammelan at Dussehra Maidan in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, on October 3, 2026, and inaugurate the State-Level Exhibition on Nyaya Sanhita. Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav will also be present on the occasion.

At the beginning of the programme, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will inaugurate the State-Level Exhibition on Nyaya Sanhita. He will thereafter visit the exhibition sections showcasing the achievements of the Madhya Pradesh Police in the implementation of the new criminal laws.

During the programme, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) will be exchanged between KRIBHCO and the Madhya Pradesh State Biodiversity Board for developing an urban forest in Bhopal under the ‘Morvan Project’. Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will also lay the foundation stones and inaugurate various important projects related to the dairy and cooperative sectors and distribute benefits to beneficiaries.

On the occasion, Shri Amit Shah will digitally lay the foundation stone for a Milk Processing Plant with a capacity of 3 lakh litres per day in Ujjain, to be established at a cost of ₹255 crore. He will also inaugurate a Product Dairy Plant in Bhopal, built at a cost of ₹16.5 crore, with a capacity of 40,000 litres per day.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation will also inaugurate a state-of-the-art State-Level Central Laboratory in Bhopal, constructed at a cost of ₹12.42 crore. In addition, the strengthening works of the Mini Dairy Plant in Shivpuri, undertaken at a cost of ₹6.5 crore, will be digitally inaugurated. These projects constitute important initiatives towards strengthening milk-processing capacity and dairy-sector infrastructure in Madhya Pradesh.

During the programme, bonus will be distributed to members of the Bhopal and Indore Milk Unions through a single click. Financial assistance will also be provided to Gaushalas through a single click. Members of Dairy Cooperative Societies will be felicitated, and a total dividend of ₹15.10 crore will be distributed among the members.

Highlighting the role of women livestock rearers in the dairy cooperative ecosystem, ‘Gopalak Didis’ will be felicitated during the Gopalak Sammelan. In addition, two sanction letters under the Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Kamdhenu Yojana will also be distributed.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance DRI cracks down on illegal wildlife trafficking; elephant ivory, leopard skin, live pangolins and tiger parts seized; 11 persons arrested Intelligence-led operations across Maharashtra expose attempts to trade in protected wildlife and wildlife derivatives Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 10:02PM by PIB Delhi Continuing its efforts to combat illegal wildlife trafficking and the illicit trade in protected wildlife products, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has, in three intelligence-led operations, seized four elephant ivory articles including…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI cracks down on illegal wildlife trafficking; elephant ivory, leopard skin, live pangolins and tiger parts seized; 11 persons arrested
Intelligence-led operations across Maharashtra expose attempts to trade in protected wildlife and wildlife derivatives
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 10:02PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its efforts to combat illegal wildlife trafficking and the illicit trade in protected wildlife products, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has, in three intelligence-led operations, seized four elephant ivory articles including intricately carved ivory articles, one leopard skin, two live pangolins, 3 kg tiger bones and two tiger canines. Eleven persons have been apprehended in the three operations.

Seized Ivory Tusks and articles

In an operation targeting illegal trade in elephant ivory, DRI officers conducted a decoy operation based on specific intelligence regarding attempts to illicitly sell four elephant tusks, including intricately carved ivory articles. The operation resulted in the recovery of the four wildlife articles and apprehension of three persons involved in the transaction. Possession without licence and trade/dealing in elephant ivory and articles made therefrom are prohibited under Section 49B of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. The seized articles and the detained persons were subsequently handed over to the jurisdictional Forest Range Officer for further investigation and necessary action.

In another intelligence led operation on 29.09.2026, DRI officers, after a surveillance, intercepted two persons near Purada village in Gondia district, Maharashtra, suspected to be attempting to sell leopard’s skin after killing it. The interception resulted recovery of one leopard skin. The leopard (Panthera pardus) is listed under Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, and the recovered skin was accordingly seized under the relevant provisions of the Act. The two persons, along with the seized leopard skin, were handed over to the Forest Range Officer, Deoria Range, Gondia, for further necessary action.

Seized Leopard skin

In a major joint operation conducted on 26–27.09.2026 in the Allapalli forest area of Maharashtra, DRI, along with the Forest Department, Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB), Mumbai and USTR Anti-Poaching Unit, intercepted six persons suspected to be involved in the illicit trade of endangered wildlife. The operation resulted in the recovery of one live adult pangolin, one live baby pangolin, 3 kg tiger bones and two tiger canines. The pangolins, protected under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 and listed in Schedule I, are also listed in Appendix I of CITES, with their international trade prohibited. Tigers and their body parts are similarly protected under Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.

The investigations and follow up searches resulted in recovery of incriminating evidence relating to the alleged poaching, possession, transportation and proposed sale of tiger body parts. The two live pangolins, tiger bones, tiger canines and two motorcycles used by the persons were seized under the provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 for further necessary action by the Forest Department.

Seized Pangolin with Baby, two Tiger canines and Tiger bones

The three operations highlight DRI's continued focus on disrupting wildlife trafficking networks at the point of illegal possession, transportation and attempted sale of protected species and their derivatives, in close coordination with specialised wildlife enforcement agencies.
