item.dc:creator: Ministry of Electronics & IT
item.description: Ministry of Electronics & IT Digital India BHASHINI Division and CAG Launch “CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad” to Enable AI-powered Multilingual Translation of Official Documents Collaboration brings Language AI into institutional translation processes, while Hindi Pakhwada activities showcase technology-enabled language engagement Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India , in collaboration with the Office of the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Digital India BHASHINI Division and CAG Launch “CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad” to Enable AI-powered Multilingual Translation of Official Documents
Collaboration brings Language AI into institutional translation processes, while Hindi Pakhwada activities showcase technology-enabled language engagement
Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), today launched “CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad”, an AI-enabled document translation solution developed by BHASHINI to support the translation of official CAG documents and audit-related reports. The solution was launched during the closing ceremony of the 74th Hindi Diwas and Hindi Pakhwada 2026 at the CAG Office, New Delhi.

 

The event was attended by Shri K. Sanjay Murthy, Comptroller and Auditor General of India, along with senior CAG officials, including Shri A. M. Bajaj, Deputy Comptroller and Auditor General; Dr. Nilotpal Goswami, Additional Deputy Comptroller and Auditor General; and Shri Atoorva Sinha, Director General, as well as other officials and dignitaries.

The launch marks an important step in bringing Language AI into institutional workflows, combining BHASHINI’s multilingual language technology capabilities with the specialised language requirements of the CAG. The initiative is designed to support translation of official and audit-related documents while complementing existing institutional processes and maintaining appropriate human oversight.

CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad has been developed as a customised Language AI solution for the CAG, with a focus on supporting consistent terminology, contextual translation and quality of output. The solution provides an AI-enabled environment for translation of official documents while addressing institutional requirements relating to security, controlled access and data sovereignty.

The collaboration reflects the broader potential of Language AI to support government institutions in making official information more accessible across languages. By integrating multilingual AI capabilities into established institutional processes, the initiative seeks to facilitate wider and more efficient access to official information in Indian languages.

The programme featured a presentation on Digital India BHASHINI’s Language AI capabilities, highlighting its applications across government and public-facing services. The event also marked the formal launch of the CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad solution at the CAG Office.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, highlighted the evolution of BHASHINI across language data and AI models, applications and use cases, and the development of a sovereign Language AI ecosystem suited to India’s linguistic diversity.

He highlighted that BHASHINI currently supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, and is being applied across a growing range of public-service use cases. These include multilingual agricultural advisory, voice-enabled grievance registration and processing, and conversational services that enable access through voice and telephone-based interfaces.

Shri K. Sanjay Murthy, Comptroller and Auditor General of India, emphasised the importance of ensuring that audit findings and reports reach citizens in languages they understand. He highlighted the potential of technology to facilitate access to audit information in local and regional languages, while complementing efforts to strengthen the use of Hindi and other Indian languages in official work.

Shri Nilotpal Goswami, Additional Deputy Comptroller & Auditor General (Rajbhasha), Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, said, “The fusion of artificial intelligence and communication has the potential to overcome linguistic barriers across geographies. By integrating language technology into our institutional processes, we can make communication more accessible, timely and effective, while strengthening the use of Indian languages in governance and official work. The CAG-BHASHINI initiative is an important step in bringing this convergence of language and technology into practice.”

 

BHASHINI and CAG collaborate on technology-enabled Hindi Pakhwada activities

The collaboration between CAG and BHASHINI also extended to the Hindi Pakhwada 2026 programme, organised from 14 to 29 September 2026. Alongside conventional Hindi language activities, the collaboration introduced technology-enabled language activities and games developed with BHASHINI, providing officers and employees an opportunity to engage with language technology in an interactive format.

A large number of officers and employees participated in various competitions and activities during the Hindi Pakhwada. The programme included activities related to official language usage, Hindi noting and drafting, translation, typing and other language-based skills, along with BHASHINI-enabled activities.The winners of the competitions were felicitated and awarded prizes during the closing ceremony. The ceremony also included the presentation of awards and certificates to the winners, recognising their participation and performance during Hindi Pakhwada.

The programme featured a presentation on the use of digital language technologies, along with demonstrations and activities aimed at familiarising officials with the growing role of technology in Hindi and Indian-language usage. The collaboration demonstrated how Language AI can support not only translation and official workflows, but also interactive language engagement and participation within government institutions.

The launch of CAG-BHASHINI Anuvaad, together with the technology-enabled Hindi Pakhwada activities, represents a broader collaboration between CAG and BHASHINI to explore practical applications of Language AI in institutional settings. The initiative brings together language technology, human expertise and institutional requirements to support greater multilingual access to official information.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 24 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, making Digital Public Infrastructure more accessible through Language AI.

****

Vinod Kumar / Dhanya Ranjan

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Union Minister Shri G. Kishan Reddy Reviews Coal India Limited’s Preparations for Special Campaign 6
Focus on Institutionalising Swachhata, Resolving Pendency, and Accelerating ‘Waste to Wealth’ & e-Waste Management
Over 1,500 Cleaning Sites Identified Across Coal PSUs; Nearly 60,000 Files Targeted for Review
Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi

 

As part of Special Campaign 6, Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister of Coal & Mines, reviewed the progress and preparations of Coal India Limited (CIL) for Special Campaign 6 along with Secretary (Coal), Chairman CIL, CMDs and other Senior officers, of Subsidiaries, aimed at institutionalising Swachhata and liquidating pendency, with a special thrust on ‘Waste to Wealth’ and ‘e-Waste Management’.

 

Key Highlights and Preparatory Initiatives

Promoting Cleanliness Awareness: South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL)

Cleanliness Awareness Walkathon at Vasant Vihar, Bilaspur, in which children enthusiastically participated and spread the message of cleanliness and environmental awareness.

 

Street play on the theme “Our Threshold, Our Waste” at the SECL Headquarters premises in Bilaspur. Through the street play, the importance of cleanliness, proper waste disposal, and individual responsibility for maintaining a clean and healthy environment in one’s surroundings were presented in an effective and engaging manner.

Identification of sites for cleaning: The Ministry of Coal, along with Coal India Limited and all Coal PSUs, has identified 1,565 sites for cleaning under Special Campaign 6, to be undertaken from 2 October to 31 October.

File Management: 19,499 physical files and 40,094 e-files have been marked for review to improve operational efficiency and ensure quick retrieval of records.

Ministry of Coal is geared up for achieving all targets within the stipulated timelines under Special Campaign 6, reinforcing the Government’s vision of efficient governance and transparency.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Home Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Home Affairs Indian security forces neutralize senior Laskhar-E-Toiba Commander, Musa aka Asif Fauji, in an intelligence-led operation in J&K Security Forces were pursuing Musa for long, and, recently a specific all-stakeholder plan for his neutralization was put in place Neutralization of Musa by Indian security forces, is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in the UT of J&K With Musa’s killing, entire group of four senior LeT Commanders operating in J&K since 2022, and responsible for several sensational attacks, stands neutralized Security Forces neutralized the three other members…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Indian security forces neutralize senior Laskhar-E-Toiba Commander, Musa aka Asif Fauji, in an intelligence-led operation in J&K
Security Forces were pursuing Musa for long, and, recently a specific all-stakeholder plan for his neutralization was put in place
Neutralization of Musa by Indian security forces, is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in the UT of J&K
With Musa’s killing, entire group of four senior LeT Commanders operating in J&K since 2022, and responsible for several sensational attacks, stands neutralized
Security Forces neutralized the three other members of the group in separate encounters of Junaid Bhat, Suleman and Yasir
Current encounter to neutralize Musa was part of an ongoing long-sustained ‘Operation Sheruwali’, started in May, 2026
Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 4:09PM by PIB Delhi

In an intelligence-led joint Security Forces operation, senior Lashkar-e-Toiba Commander, Musa aka Asif Fauji, was neutralized at Gurwatkalan, Khansahib PS of Budgam District, J&K. Security Forces were pursuing Musa for long, and, recently a specific all-stakeholder plan for his neutralization was put in place after technical and human intelligence about his movement and presence were received.

Neutralization of Musa by Indian security forces is a serious blow to LeT ecosystem in the UT of J&K. With Musa’s killing, the entire group of four senior LeT Commanders operating in the UT since 2022, and responsible for sensational attacks, like Halan attack (Aug 2023), DKG attack (Dec 2023), Kandi attack (May 2023), Shahsitar attack (May 2024), Shiv Khori attack (June 2024), Gagangir attack (Oct 2024), Bootapathri attack (Oct 2024) and Baisaran attack (Apr 2025), stands neutralized. The three other members of the group were neutralized by Security Forces in separate encounters of Junaid Bhat (Dec 03, 2024, Dachigam), Suleman (July 28, 2025, OP Mahadev), and Yasir (Sep 04, 2026, Op Asdhar). The current encounter to neutralize Musa was part of an ongoing long-sustained operation.  

Over the past few years, all security agencies—such as the Jammu & Kashmir Police, the Indian Army, and the CAPF—have been conducting counter-terrorism operations in close coordination, yielding positive results.

*****

item.title: In a major success in the fight against drugs, 526 kilograms of methamphetamine and heroin seized from an Iranian boat in India's EEZ, and 5 Pakistani nationals arrested during a joint operation involving Gujarat ATS, Indian Coast Guard, and central intelligence agencies, says Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Home Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Home Affairs In a major success in the fight against drugs, 526 kilograms of methamphetamine and heroin seized from an Iranian boat in India's EEZ, and 5 Pakistani nationals arrested during a joint operation involving Gujarat ATS, Indian Coast Guard, and central intelligence agencies, says Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah Modi govt. is determined to shield its youth from the scourge of drugs Upholding a stellar example of coordination and cooperation among agencies the 16-day long operation also seized an Iranian boat The operation reflects the strength of intelligence-led,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
In a major success in the fight against drugs, 526 kilograms of methamphetamine and heroin seized from an Iranian boat in India's EEZ, and 5 Pakistani nationals arrested during a joint operation involving Gujarat ATS, Indian Coast Guard, and central intelligence agencies, says Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah
Modi govt. is determined to shield its youth from the scourge of drugs
Upholding a stellar example of coordination and cooperation among agencies the 16-day long operation also seized an Iranian boat
The operation reflects the strength of intelligence-led, inter-agency coordination in securing India’s maritime borders
Further investigation underway to identify the wider network and its intended receivers
A safer, healthier and Nasha-Mukt Bharat remains our shared national resolve
Modi government’s Vision Document on Drug Control (2026–2029) provides a comprehensive roadmap to strengthen enforcement, disrupt drug networks and protect our youth and society from narcotics
Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today said that in a major success in the fight against drugs 526 kilograms of methamphetamine and heroin were seized from an Iranian boat within India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), and five Pakistani nationals were arrested, during a joint operation involving the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), the Indian Coast Guard, and central intelligence agencies.

In a post on X, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated, “Modi govt. is determined to shield its youth from the scourge of drugs. In a joint operation by Gujarat ATS, Indian Coast Guard and Central intelligence agencies, 526 kg of Methamphetamine and Heroin has been seized from an Iranian boat in India’s EEZ, 160 NM northwest of Lakshadweep and 490 NM southwest of Mumbai. Five Pakistani nationals have been arrested, with further investigation underway to identify the wider network and its intended receivers. Upholding a stellar example of coordination and cooperation among agencies the 16-day long operation also seized an Iranian boat.” 

Modi govt. is determined to shield its youth from the scourge of drugs. In a joint operation by Gujarat ATS, Indian Coast Guard and Central intelligence agencies, 526 kg of Methamphetamine and Heroin has been seized from an Iranian boat in India’s EEZ, 160 NM northwest of Lakshadweep and 490 NM southwest of Mumbai. Five Pakistani nationals have been arrested, with further investigation underway to identify the wider network and its intended receivers. Upholding a stellar example of coordination and cooperation among agencies the 16 day long operation also seized an Iranian boat.

— Amit Shah (@AmitShah) September 30, 2026

The operation, conducted from 14th to 30th September, reflects the strength of intelligence-led, inter-agency coordination in securing India’s maritime borders.

The Vision Document on Drug Control (2026–2029) unveiled by the Modi government provides a comprehensive roadmap to strengthen enforcement, disrupt drug networks and protect our youth and society from narcotics.

A safer, healthier and Nasha-Mukt Bharat remains our shared national resolve.

 

****

Targeted support can also create opportunities for beneficiaries to inspire others in their communities to pursue advanced…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Assistance to Academic Excellence
KarimNagar Telangana’s Minakashi’s Journey towards Higher Education, Social Empowerment
Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 3:46PM by PIB Delhi

Financial assistance can play an important role in enabling students from disadvantaged communities to pursue higher education, overcome financial constraints and build confidence to achieve their academic aspirations. Targeted support can also create opportunities for beneficiaries to inspire others in their communities to pursue advanced education.

Minakashi, a 36-year-old PhD Research Scholar belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) community, aspired to build a career in teaching, research and the scientific field at a reputed university. Financial instability, however, posed a significant challenge in continuing her higher studies.

Coming from a community where access to higher education remains limited, Minakashi faced barriers related to financial resources, confidence and access to opportunities. The lack of adequate support made it difficult for many members of her community to pursue higher education with confidence.

During 2022–25, under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Minakashi received financial assistance of Rs. 11 lakh. The support enabled her to continue and complete her higher education without the burden of financial constraints.

Today, Minakashi stands as an example of how targeted financial assistance can create opportunities for academic advancement and social empowerment. Her journey has helped inspire other students from economically disadvantaged and socially marginalized communities to pursue higher education with greater confidence.

Minakshi’s experience reflects the impact of financial assistance under the NFSC Scheme in enabling students to overcome financial barriers, continue higher education and contribute to the aspirations of others in their communities.

Through the support received under the NFSC Scheme, Minakashi has transformed financial constraints into an opportunity for academic growth, while becoming an inspiration for other students to pursue higher education and work towards a more empowered future.

Talking about the financial support and its benefits, Minakshi said, “The NFSC Scheme gave me the financial support I needed to complete my PhD. Today, I am not just fulfilling my dream, but also helping other students from my community to dream bigger.”

The assistance extended through the NFSC Scheme helped Minakashi strengthen her confidence and pursue her academic goals. During her academic journey, she also contributed to educating students who aspired to pursue higher education but faced financial difficulties. Her experience encouraged students from disadvantaged communities to consider higher education as an achievable pathway.

*****

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance Special Campaign 6.0: DIPAM Engages MSTC to Auction and Responsibly Recycle Departmental E-Waste The Partnership aims for Scientific and Eco-Friendly E-Waste Disposal under Special Campaign 6.0 Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 3:31PM by PIB Delhi As part of its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata and ensuring environmentally responsible management of electronic waste, the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) has engaged MSTC Limited, a Miniratna Category-I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Steel, for the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Special Campaign 6.0: DIPAM Engages MSTC to Auction and Responsibly Recycle Departmental E-Waste
The Partnership aims for Scientific and Eco-Friendly E-Waste Disposal under Special Campaign 6.0
Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 3:31PM by PIB Delhi

As part of its commitment to institutionalising Swachhata and ensuring environmentally responsible management of electronic waste, the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) has engaged MSTC Limited, a Miniratna Category-I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Steel, for the scientific collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste generated in the Department.

This step is being taken under Special Campaign 6 (2nd – 31st October 2026), which has a special focus on “Effective Collection, Segregation and Disposal of E-Waste” in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

MSTC’s specialised e-auction platform will facilitate transparent and compliant disposal of obsolete electronic equipment such as computers, printers, servers and other IT assets. The engagement will not only free up valuable office space but will also ensure that e-waste is channelled through authorised recyclers, thereby converting waste into resource while generating revenue for the Government.

DIPAM remains committed to the larger goals of Special Campaign 6 – saturation of cleanliness in Government offices, reduction of pendency, and promotion of sustainable practices across its offices.

*****

Sanjay Roy/Divya Ann Mathew

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Cabinet approves Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28
Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 3:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the increase in the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for all mandated Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28.

Government has increased the Minimum Support Prices (MSP) of Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28, to ensure remunerative prices to the growers for their produce. The absolute highest increase in MSP has been announced for Safflower at Rs.675 per quintal followed by Rapeseed & Mustard at Rs.413 per quintal. For Lentil (Masur), barley, gram, and wheat, there is an increase of Rs.390 per quintal, Rs.136 per quintal, Rs.83 per quintal and Rs.25 per quintal respectively.

*Refers to cost which includes all paid out costs such as those incurred on account of hired human labour, bullock labour/machine labour, rent paid for leased in land, expenses incurred on use of material inputs like seeds, fertilizers, manures, irrigation charges, depreciation on implements and farm buildings, interest on working capital, diesel/electricity for operation of pump sets etc., miscellaneous expenses and imputed value of family labour.

The increase in MSP for mandated Rabi Crops for Marketing Season 2027-28 is in line with the Union Budget 2018-19 announcement of fixing the MSP at a level of at least 1.5 times of the All-India weighted average Cost of Production. The expected margin over All-India weighted average cost of production is 106 percent for wheat, followed by 96 percent for rapeseed & mustard; 92 per cent for lentil; 59 per cent for gram; 58 percent for barley; and 50 percent for safflower. This increased MSP of rabi crops will ensure remunerative prices to the farmers and incentivise crop diversification.

In the recent years, Government has been promoting the cultivation of crops, other than cereals such as pulses and oilseeds by offering a higher MSP for these crops. 

The procurement of wheat during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to 3715 LMT as compared to 2254 LMT during 2004-05 to 2013-14. The procurement of 6 Rabi crops during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to 3921 LMT as compared to 2302 LMT during 2004-05 to 2013-14.

The MSP amount paid to Wheat growing famers during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to Rs. 7.31 Lakh crore as compared to Rs.2.56  Lakh crore during 2004-05 to 2013-14. The MSP amount paid to 6 Rabi crops growing farmers during 2014-15 to 2025-26 has increased to Rs.8.36 Lakh crore as compared to Rs.2.65 Lakh crore during 2004-05 to 2013-14.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Home Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Home Affairs Cabinet approves One Network, Smarter Traffic: Delhi Moves to Real-Time Traffic Management Rs.1,789.52 crore approved for Intelligent Traffic Management System for Delhi AI-enabled adaptive traffic signals, technology-based enforcement and real-time traffic information to make travel safer, smoother and more efficient 42 traffic corridors of Delhi to be covered in three phases System to facilitate priority movement of ambulances and quicker response to congestion and road incidents Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi The Cabinet…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Cabinet approves One Network, Smarter Traffic: Delhi Moves to Real-Time Traffic Management
Rs.1,789.52 crore approved for Intelligent Traffic Management System for Delhi
AI-enabled adaptive traffic signals, technology-based enforcement and real-time traffic information to make travel safer, smoother and more efficient 42 traffic corridors of Delhi to be covered in three phases
System to facilitate priority movement of ambulances and quicker response to congestion and road incidents
Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved implementation of the ITMS Project by Delhi Police at an estimated cost of Rs.1,789.52 crore, inclusive of taxes. The project will cover 42 identified traffic corridors and will be implemented in three phases over 24 months, followed by five years of operation and maintenance.

As part of the wider efforts of the Central Government and the Government of NCT of Delhi to improve traffic management, transport infrastructure and urban mobility in the National Capital, a major technology-led initiative will now be taken up through the Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS). The project will enable Delhi’s existing road network to be managed more intelligently through real-time traffic data, adaptive traffic signals, automated enforcement and integrated command-and-control systems.

Delhi has around 71 lakh active registered vehicles. Vehicular growth has substantially outpaced expansion of road infrastructure, while traffic regulation continues to depend significantly on fixed signal timings and manual intervention. The ITMS seeks to make better use of the available road capacity by enabling traffic management to respond dynamically to actual conditions on the road.

Benefits:

  • Smarter traffic signals and smoother movement: Adaptive Traffic Control Systems will dynamically adjust signal timings according to prevailing traffic conditions and coordinate signals along identified corridors, helping reduce avoidable stoppages and delays.
  • Priority for ambulances and emergency vehicles: The system will facilitate green corridors and priority movement for emergency vehicles, enabling faster passage through congested stretches.
  • Faster response to congestion and accidents: Real-time detection of congestion, slow-moving traffic and road incidents will enable quicker diversions and operational response by Delhi Police.
  • Timely information for commuters: Variable Message Sign boards and digital platforms will provide information on congestion, diversions, parking availability and traffic conditions. Information may also be shared with navigation service providers, helping commuters make better travel choices.
  • More consistent and technology-based enforcement: The system will strengthen automated detection of violations such as red-light and stop-line violations, speeding, wrong-way driving, non-use of helmets and seat belts, illegal parking and use of mobile phones while driving. AI-based analytics will also assist in identifying stolen, hot-listed and blacklisted vehicles, repeat violators and vehicles connected with hit-and-run incidents.

Integrated city-wide traffic management:

Traffic regulation, enforcement and information dissemination will be brought together on a common platform through Traffic Command and Control Centres, supported by secure Data Centre and Disaster Recovery infrastructure. The system will follow open standards and APIs to enable future integration and scalability.

The project will cover 1,092 Adaptive Traffic Control System and 1,029 enforcement locations. Implementation will be performance-driven, with each subsequent phase to be taken up after evaluation of the preceding phase against prescribed testing, commissioning, acceptance and performance parameters.

Delhi Police will implement the project through a Master System Integrator selected through competitive bidding. C-DAC will provide technical support as Project Management Consultant, including technical scrutiny, monitoring, validation and acceptance during implementation and operation and maintenance.

The ITMS will complement ongoing efforts to improve Delhi’s road and transport infrastructure by providing the technology and real-time intelligence required to use the existing road network more efficiently. The project is expected to contribute to smoother traffic movement, safer roads, quicker incident response, more effective enforcement and a more predictable travel experience for citizens.

 

****

PIB Backgrounder
UNION PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
A Century of Meritocracy and Inclusion
Posted On: 30 SEP 2026 11:34AM by PIB Delhi

 

On 1 October 2026, the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) completes one hundred years. Its institutional journey began on 1 October 1926, when India’s first Public Service Commission was constituted - an advisory body whose Chairman and Members were appointed by the Secretary of State in London. Over the century that followed, the Commission evolved in structure, status and responsibilities, becoming what it is today - an independent constitutional body.

 

The Road to 1926

The principle that entry into public service should rest on merit rather than patronage took formal shape in 1855, when the Indian Civil Service (ICS) examination was instituted in London, replacing the East India Company’s system of nomination with open competition. For most Indians, however, the door remained nearly impossible to open. The examination was held only in London, in English, and tested candidates on subjects such as Greek and Latin - not because these were needed to govern a district in Bengal or Punjab, but because they favoured those educated in the British system.

In 1862, 21-year-old Satyendranath Tagore, elder brother of Rabindranath Tagore, sailed from Calcutta to England to sit an examination his own country would not let him take at home. He cleared it in 1863 and joined the service in 1864 - the first Indian in what the British called the “heaven-born service”. He served for over thirty years in the Bombay Presidency. Six years after his success, Surendranath Banerjee, Behari Lal Gupta and Romesh Chunder Dutt followed. The maximum age for the examination was, however, progressively reduced from 23 to 19, leaving Indian candidates little time to prepare. By 1919, only 78 of the 1,255 ICS officers were Indian.

Sustained nationalist demands brought gradual change. The Government of India Act, 1919, enacted after the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, provided for a Public Service Commission. In 1922, the ICS examination was held in India for the first time, at Allahabad, alongside London. In 1928 the Indian centre moved to Delhi. In 1924, the Lee Commission, chaired by Arthur Hamilton Lee, recommended the immediate establishment of a statutory Public Service Commission. It also proposed that of every ten new entrants, four would be British, four Indian and two Indians promoted from the provincial services - on paper a path to parity, in practice a guaranteed 40 per cent of every intake for the British, by birth rather than by competition.

The Commission was established under the Public Service Commission (Functions) Rules, 1926, framed under Sections 96B and 96C of the 1919 Act. Sir Ross Barker, a member of the Home Civil Service of the United Kingdom, was its first Chairman, assisted by four Members, and the Commission was housed at Metcalfe House, Delhi. Its limited powers drew sustained criticism from leaders of the freedom movement. Yet a permanent recruiting body now existed in India, seated and staffed in India - which is why the Commission dates its history from 1926.

The Constitutional Mandate

On 22 August 1949, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Chairman of the Drafting Committee, moved the draft articles on the Union and State Public Service Commissions in the Constituent Assembly. They became Part XIV (Articles 315–323) of the Constitution. In his valedictory address on 26 November 1949, Dr. Rajendra Prasad emphasised that the independence of the Public Service Commissions was essential to ensure impartiality in public appointments and to guard against jobbery, nepotism and favouritism.

Article

What it provides

315

Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States, with provision for a Joint Commission for two or more States

316

Chairman and Members appointed by the President

317

Removal or suspension of a Member only by order of the President, after an inquiry by the Supreme Court

318

Power to make regulations on the conditions of service of Members and staff

319

Restrictions on holding office after ceasing to be a Member; the Chairman is ineligible for further employment under the Government of India or a State

320

Functions: conducting examinations for appointment to the services of the Union, and advising on methods of recruitment, promotions and disciplinary matters

321

Power of Parliament or a State Legislature to extend the Commission’s functions

322

Expenses of the Commission charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

323

Annual report to the President; cases where the Commission’s advice was not accepted, with reasons, laid before Parliament

What the Commission does

  • Recruitment by examination: The Civil Services, Indian Forest Service, Engineering Services, Combined Medical Services, National Defence Academy & Naval Academy, Combined Defence Services and Central Armed Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) examinations, among others.
  • Recruitment by selection: Interviews and recruitment tests for specialist posts requisitioned by Ministries and Departments.
  • Advice to Government: On Recruitment Rules, promotions through Departmental Promotion Committees, induction into the All India Services and disciplinary cases. In 2023-24, it processed the records of 24,581 officers for promotion, and 532 officers were inducted into the All India Services.
  • Police leadership: Since 2012–13, pursuant to the Supreme Court’s order of 22 September 2006 in Prakash Singh vs Union of India, the Commission empanels senior IPS officers for appointment as Director General of Police/Head of Police Force in the States.

 

Landmark Events: 1926–2026

Foundations: 1926–1949

Year

Milestone

1935

Government of India Act, 1935 transfers the power of appointment to the Governor-General, provides for a Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs, and makes consultation with the Commission mandatory on recruitment, appointments, promotions, disciplinary cases and service rules.

1937

Renamed the Federal Public Service Commission (1 April).

1938

Combined Competitive Examinations begin for several services - the start of unified, multi-service recruitment.

1940

Indians (625) outnumber Europeans (575) in the ICS for the first time.

1947

Shri H.K. Kripalani becomes the first Indian Chairman.

 

First examination after Independence held in December; the ICS gives way to the IAS.

1948

First batch of Indian Foreign Service officers recruited through the combined examination.

Building the Republic’s Services: 1950–1979

Year

Milestone

1950

Federal PSC becomes the Union Public Service Commission on 26 January, with Shri R.N. Banerjee as Chairman.

1950–51

First regular recruitment to the All-India Services under the Constitution: 29 candidates recommended for the IAS and 31 for the IPS.

1951

All-India Services Act enacted.

1966

Indian Forest Service constituted as the third All India Service; first selection in 1967.

1969

Eighth Schedule languages introduced as options for the Essay and General Studies papers of the Civil Services Examination.

1976

Golden Jubilee. Applications cross one lakh for the first time.

 

The D.S. Kothari Committee proposes a three-stage examination.

1977

First Combined Medical Services Examination.

1978

Commission adopts computers to process applications, answer sheets and records.

1979

Three-stage Civil Services Examination - Preliminary, Main and Interview - introduced.

 

Eighth Schedule languages formalised in the Main Examination; London centre discontinued.

 

Reform and Modernisation: 1985–2010

Year

Milestone

1985

Sanctioned strength raised to a Chairman and ten Members.

1988–89

Satish Chandra Committee recommends more centres, a 200-mark essay, negative marking in the Preliminary Examination and more marks for the interview.

1989

Optical Mark Recognition (OMR) technology introduced.

1992

Smt. Rose Millian Bathew Kharbuli becomes the first woman Chairperson.

1993

Essay paper introduced in the Civil Services (Main) Examination; interview marks raised from 250 to 300.

1994

Medical Science added as an optional subject.

2000

Online Recruitment Application (ORA) system launched, following the SAMPERA common application form (1999–2000); by 2010, applications for several examinations were fully online.

2003

First Central Police Forces (Assistant Commandants) Examination held (12 October).

2005

New office building, ‘Ayog Sachivalaya’, inaugurated (22 December).

2009

Foundation Day Lecture series on ‘Governance and Public Service’ inaugurated by President Smt. Pratibha Devisingh Patil (12 November); Indian Corporate Law Service added to the Civil Services Examination.

2010

UPSC hosts the Conference of Chiefs of Public Service Commissions of SAARC countries (20–22 November).

 

Digital, Transparent and Inclusive: 2011–2026

Year

Milestone

2011

Civil Services Aptitude Test (CSAT) introduced; Single Window System (1 September).

2013

Civil Services (Main) restructured: four General Studies papers, including Ethics, Integrity and Aptitude, and one optional subject. First Computer-Based Recruitment Tests. IFoS screening through the CS (Preliminary) Examination.

2015

CSAT made a qualifying paper (33 per cent).

2017

Engineering Services Examination becomes three-stage; seven-day online window for representations on questions.

2018

Query-Based Marks Information System (1 June).

2019

Dedicated Control Room for year-round monitoring of examinations.

2021

Women admitted to the NDA & NA Examination for the first time - NDA & NA Examination (II), 2021, held on 14 November 2021.

2022

Existing four Group A Railway services under the Civil Services Examination unified as the Indian Railway Management Service.

Developments in 2025 and 2026 are listed in Section 7.

Facts and Figures

The scale of the Commission

The scale and complexity of the work handled by UPSC have increased significantly over the years, as applications across examinations and recruitment by selection grew from 42,727 in 1950-51 to a peak of 45,10,044 in 2022-23 - an increase of more than a hundredfold. In that year, the Commission conducted 15 examinations (33,51,916 applications) and received 233 requisitions for 4,411 posts under recruitment by selection (11,58,128 applications).

Then and Now

Indicator

Then

Now

Change

Examination centres

8 (1950)

86 (2026)

Over 10×

Women recommended in Civil Services Examination

3 of 83 (1952)

299 of 958 (2025)

About 100×

SC candidates recommended in Civil Services Examination

9 (1955)

158 (2025)

About 18×

ST candidates recommended in Civil Services Examination

2 (1956-57)

73 (2025)

About 37×

SC applicants, all examinations

1,713  (1956-57)

4,51,243 (2023-24)

About 382×

ST applicants, all examinations

82 (1956-57)

1,47,106 (2023-24)

About 1794×

PwBD candidates recommended in Civil Services Examination

3 (2002)

42 (2025)

14×

Disciplinary cases advised on

53 (1950-51)

446 (2023-24)

About 8×

Inclusion in numbers

  • Women: Between 1949 and 1951, only one woman was selected for the Indian Foreign Service and two for the IAS. Women made up 3.6 per cent of those recommended in 1952 and 31.2 per cent in CSE 2025, when they also secured 11 of the top 25 ranks.
  • Indian languages at the interview: in 1970-71, the Commission informed the Government that the Personality Test could be conducted only in English. The position changed in 1980-81, and candidates may now answer in an Indian language with an interpreter provided by the Commission; 803 chose to do so in 2010-11 and 307 in 2023-24.

 

Anecdotes

Short stories from the Commission’s century.

Where the ‘steel frame’ speech was made

Metcalfe House, built in 1835 by Sir Thomas Metcalfe, has a second claim to history. On 21 April 1947, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel addressed the first batch of civil service probationers there and described the civil services as the “steel frame of India”. The date is now observed every year as Civil Services Day.

 

A Maharaja’s transit house

Dholpur House on Shahjahan Road was built in 1920 in the Art Deco style by Maharaja Rana Udaybhanu Singh of Dholpur, as his residence during visits to Delhi. After Dholpur State merged with the Union on 7 April 1949, the building became government property. Three years later, in 1952, it became the Commission’s permanent headquarters.

 

One among eighty

In 1972, Kiran Bedi became the first woman selected by the Commission for the Indian Police Service, a service that had never had a woman officer. Of the eighty vacancies that year, she was the only woman.

 

Forms in the newspaper

In 1989, when slow post made it difficult for application forms to reach remote areas, the Commission printed them directly in newspapers. In 1984, when heavy snowfall cut off Kangra, it extended the application deadline by two weeks for affected aspirants.

 

A sun on a stamp

On 8 November 1977, the Posts and Telegraphs Department issued a 25-paise stamp for the Commission’s Golden Jubilee. It showed the sun - symbolising impartiality and equal opportunity for all - with the national tricolour. For the Platinum Jubilee, inaugurated by Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on 14 December 2001, the Department of Posts issued a First Day Cover.

 

DID YOU KNOW?

  • The UPSC Museum, opened on 11 November 2016, is free and open to the public on weekdays from 9:30 am to 6:30 pm; a 360-degree virtual tour is available on the Commission’s website.
  • The age limit has travelled a long way. As late as 1988, an expert committee recommended keeping the Civil Services Examination age band at 21 to 26 years. The limits of 32 years for General candidates, 35 for OBC and 37 for SC and ST candidates, with up to ten years more for Persons with Disabilities, were fixed in 2014, when two extra attempts were also allowed.
  • Candidates who had appeared in the Civil Services Examination 2011 were given one more attempt in CSE 2015, whatever their age or the number of attempts already used.
  • The Commission has not always recruited only for the Union. In 1960-61, under Article 320, it agreed to recruit for bodies such as the Delhi Municipal Corporation, the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation and the Territorial Councils of the Union Territories.
  • Open competition lapsed during the Second World War. The London examination was held for the last time in 1939, officers for 1940, 1941 and 1942 were nominated directly, and recruitment through the British Civil Service Commission stopped altogether after 1943.
  • In the draft Constitution, the provisions on Public Service Commissions were numbered Articles 284 and 285 when Dr. B.R. Ambedkar moved them in the Constituent Assembly.

Case Studies: How the Machinery Works

Every morning in Mumbai, around 5,000 dabbawalas collect nearly two lakh home-cooked lunches and deliver each to the right desk by lunchtime, using nothing more than a colour code chalked on the lid. The Commission solves a comparable problem every year, at far higher stakes: the right question paper must reach the right candidate at the right minute, and every answer must then be judged on merit alone. The following case studies explain how.

Case Study 1:  The right paper to the right candidate

A candidate makes only one choice: the city. Within that city, the system allots the venue and the room, so that by the day of the examination every candidate has a unique address - city, venue, room, candidate - known in advance only to the system. Candidates in the same room may be writing different papers - in the Civil Services Main Examination alone, candidates choose from 48 optional subjects - so each sealed packet must carry exactly the papers needed at that venue, sorted room by room.

Case Study 2:  Setting a paper no one has seen

Question papers are built from question banks prepared by academic experts who work in anonymity under a strict code of confidentiality. No single expert sets a whole paper, and no expert knows which questions will be used, or when. In constructing a paper, the Commission ensures that it covers the entire syllabus, that its difficulty is balanced, and that no question has been asked in any previous UPSC examination.

The whole apparatus rests on the principle of ‘need to know’: no single person - not even the Chairman - sees the full picture.

Case Study 3:  Securing the examination hall

In collaboration with the National e-Governance Division, the Commission piloted AI-enabled facial authentication - matching a candidate’s live image with the application photograph - at select centres in Gurugram during the NDA & NA (II) and CDS (II) Examinations on 14 September 2025. It was implemented at scale at the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination on 24 May 2026, where face authentication was carried out for all of about 5.50 lakh candidates through invigilators’ mobile phones, taking about 6–8 seconds per candidate.

Ahead of the CS (Preliminary) Examination 2026, a scan of fifteen years of candidate data identified and rejected 569 applicants who had furnished false information to claim extra attempts.

Case Study 4:  Recruiting at the speed of need

The Commission has repeatedly scaled up when the nation required it, without lowering its standards. In July 1948, a Special Recruitment Board recruited experienced personnel aged 27 to 45 into the IAS and IPS on the basis of records and interviews. In 1956–57, a special drive screened over 22,000 candidates. In 1958, a Special Recruitment Board selected 197 scientists and technologists - including applicants from overseas - for a national Pool whose strength rose to 500 by 1962. During the 1962 emergency, an Emergency Commission filled 1,353 defence-related posts in two months.

During COVID-19, with train services disrupted, the Commission reimbursed airfare to interview candidates as a one-time measure, requested States to let candidates with e-summon letters move through restricted zones, helped with lodging and transport, and handed each candidate a sealed kit of mask, face shield, sanitiser and gloves.

Case Study 5:  Inclusion by design

Access comes first. The Commission introduced scribes for visually impaired candidates in 1994, and today the right to a scribe and extra time is an entitlement for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities, who are also allotted the centre of their choice, may bring an escort, and are assisted by a facilitator at interviews. Women candidates receive fee exemptions. Age relaxations have been extended to those whose preparation was disrupted by events beyond their control - freedom fighters of the Goa liberation (1961–62), Indians displaced by the Bangladesh Liberation War and the Uganda-Zanzibar crisis (1971–72), and Indians affected by the Gulf War (1991).

Fairness follows: an evaluation system, from written papers to the interview board, that is blind to identity. The Commission did not write the policy of reservation, but it built the national platform that implements it, including the Economically Weaker Sections category from CSE 2019 and a separate transgender category in its Online Recruitment Application form from 2020.

Case Study 6:  Merit beyond the merit list: Pratibha Setu

Candidates who clear every stage of an examination but narrowly miss the final list are not lost to public service. Under the Public Disclosure Scheme, in force since 20 August 2018 and first used for the Combined Medical Services Examination, 2017, the details of such willing candidates were made available to employers. Revamped and renamed Pratibha Setu on 9 June 2025, it connects them with verified employers, including Ministries, PSUs, autonomous bodies and private organisations.

Recent Updates

When

Development

Details

May 2025

Universal Registration Number

Revamped portal at upsconline.nic.in replaces One-Time Registration; one persistent identity across all examinations; profiles can be completed in advance.

2025

Randomised interview boards

Introduced from the Combined Medical Services Examination, 2025, with software setting the calling sequence.

2025

Email alerts for institutions

Educational and professional institutions can subscribe to alerts on recruitment advertisements by writing to ra-upsc[at]gov[dot]in.

From 1 Feb 2026

Candidate Helpdesk

30-channel IP-based call centre with two levels of escalation; more than 50,000 calls handled.

2026

New examination centres

Bhubaneswar (10,656 applications), Kanpur (6,938) and Meerut (5,902) added for CS (P) 2026, taking its centres from 80 to 83; Alwar, Hisar and Kinnaur added for NDA & NA (II) 2026.

2026

Provisional answer key

Provisional answer key for Civil Services (Preliminary) examination published soon after the examination; representations through the online QPRep portal.

2026

Online DPC system

Paperless platform for Departmental Promotion Committee proposals from about 101 Ministries, Departments and organisations under development.

2026

Technology and security

Officers trained in emerging technologies, including AI, through NIELIT; High-Level Network Committee constituted for IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

 

The Commission Today

The Commission is headed by Chairman Dr. Ajay Kumar (since 15 May 2025). Its eight Members are Lt. Gen. Raj Shukla (Retd.), Ms. Suman Sharma, Shri Bidyut Behari Swain, Dr. Dinesh Dasa, Shri Sheel Vardhan Singh, Shri Sanjay Verma, Smt. Sujata Chaturvedi and Smt. Anuradha Prasad. Three of the eight Members are women - a composition that reflects how far the institution has travelled in a hundred years.

 

“An institution that has endured for a hundred years does so not because it resists change, but because it knows what must never change.”

— Dr. Ajay Kumar, Chairman, UPSC

 

For a hundred years, the Commission has carried one of the nation’s most consequential responsibilities: to recognise merit, uphold fairness and ensure that opportunity reaches beyond privilege, geography, language or circumstance. A century ago, the struggle was for the right of Indians to compete. Today, the task is to ensure that this right genuinely reaches every deserving Indian who wishes to serve the nation.

Reference

  • Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Legal Affairs Dept Holds E-Waste Awareness Workshop under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 10:08PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, 29 September 2026: As part of Special Campaign 6 and Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, the Department of Legal Aﬀairs organized an awareness workshop on ‘E-waste Management’ at Kartavya Bhavan-2, New Delhi, on 28 September 2026.

The workshop was attended by Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Department of Legal Aﬀairs, along with officers and officials of the Department. The workshop aimed to sensitise participants about the growing importance of responsible management of electronic waste and encourage environmentally sustainable practices in day-to-day life and workplace.

Addressing the participants, Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Department of Legal Aﬀairs, highlighted the importance of responsible e-waste management and emphasised the need for greater awareness regarding the proper handling and disposal of electronic waste. He stressed the significance of adopting sustainable practices and collective responsibility to minimise the adverse impact of e-waste on the environment.

The workshop provided participants with useful information on various aspects of e-waste management, including proper segregation, safe collection, responsible disposal and recycling of electronic items. The participants were also sensitised to the 3R approach — Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, which encourages reducing the generation of e-waste, reusing electronic products wherever feasible and ensuring their recycling through appropriate channels.

The session also highlighted the importance of responsible disposal of discarded electronic devices and components, while creating awareness about the environmental benefits of adopting sustainable consumption and waste-management practices.

The awareness initiative forms part of the Department’s eﬀorts under Special Campaign 6 and Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 to promote cleanliness, sustainability and responsible waste management. It also reinforced the message that eﬀective e-waste management requires active participation and awareness at both the individual and institutional levels.

The Department of Legal Aﬀairs remains committed to promoting a cleaner, greener and more sustainable workplace through awareness, responsible practices and active participation of its officers and officials.

 

 

 

 

 

***

Samrat/Pranab/Sagar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Felicitates 20 Award-Winning Artists at National Exhibition of Arts
65th National Art Exhibition Receives Over 6,000 Entries; 270 Artists Selected Through Two-Tier Jury Process
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 9:42PM by PIB Delhi

The 65th National Exhibition of Art, organised by the Lalit Kala Akademi, was held on September 29, 2026, in New Delhi. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of  Culture and Tourism, Government of India, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India; Shri K.K. Mishra, Joint Secretary (Akademies), Ministry of Culture; and Shri Rajeev Kumar, Secretary, Lalit Kala Akademi, along with Padma Shri awardees Shri Sudharak Olwe, Shri Sudarshan Patnaik, and Shri Ashok Kumar Vishwas were present on the occasion.

On the occasion, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and other dignitaries viewed artworks created from waste materials during the ‘Seva Hi Sanskriti’ workshops organised at various centres of the Lalit Kala Akademi.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat highlighted the significance of bringing together creativity and sustainability. He said that the ‘Seva Hi Sanskriti’ initiative, organised on the occasion of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s birthday, demonstrates how creativity and the spirit of service can come together meaningfully. He appreciated the Lalit Kala Akademi’s efforts across its various verticals, including the ‘Waste to Wonder’ initiative, which gives discarded materials a new artistic expression and highlights the role of art in promoting sustainability.

Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, highlighted the importance of providing wider opportunities and greater visibility to artists and contemporary Indian art. He invited members of the public, art enthusiasts and visitors to view the 65th National Exhibition of Art at Rabindra Bhawan, New Delhi, which has been extended until October 31, 2026. He encouraged people to visit the exhibition and experience the diverse artistic expressions and contemporary trends represented by artists from across the country.

Shri Rajeev Kumar, Secretary, Lalit Kala Akademi, highlighted the national reach and evolution of the National Exhibition of Art. He said that the 65th edition received more than 6,000 entries, out of which 270 artists were selected through a two-tier jury process. He also highlighted the awards presented as part of the exhibition and the Akademi’s continued efforts to recognise and promote artistic talent from across the country.

A monograph on Abdul Aziz Raiba, edited by Shri Ram Gopal Khadilkar, was also released on the occasion. An eminent modern Indian painter, Raiba was known for his bold lines, vibrant colours and distinctive fusion of Indian traditional and modern art.

During the programme, the Union Minister felicitated 20 award-winning artists. The awards recognise their creative contributions to the field of Indian visual arts.

Following the programme, the Chief Guest and other dignitaries visited the National Exhibition of Art at the Lalit Kala Gallery. The exhibition reflects the Lalit Kala Akademi’s continued endeavour to recognise, promote and provide wider visibility to artistic talent from different parts of the country.

M Annadurai

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister congratulates Pooja on winning Bronze in Women’s High Jump at Asian Games 2026
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 9:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has congratulated Pooja on winning the Bronze medal in the Women’s High Jump at the Asian Games 2026.

The Prime Minister said that this is India’s first medal in the event at the Asian Games in over two decades and described it as a memorable achievement.

Shri Modi extended his best wishes to Pooja for her future endeavours.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister’s Office said;

“A proud moment for Indian athletics!

Congratulations to Pooja on winning the Bronze medal in the Women’s High Jump at the Asian Games 2026. This is India’s first medal in the event at the Asian Games since over two decades. It’s truly a memorable achievement. Best wishes for her upcoming endeavours: PM @narendramodi”

 

A proud moment for Indian athletics!

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
India and Republic of Korea Hold 10th Joint Committee Meeting on Defence Industries and Logistics Cooperation
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 9:31PM by PIB Delhi

The 10th India-Republic of Korea Joint Committee Meeting (JCM) on Defence Industries and Logistics Cooperation was held in New Delhi on September 29, 2026. Both countries reviewed the ongoing bilateral cooperation in defence industries and logistics and discussed avenues to further strengthen and expand defence ties.

The discussions provided an opportunity to exchange views on enhancing cooperation between the defence industries of the two countries and promoting greater engagement in defence production and logistics.

The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Dinesh Mahur, Additional Secretary (Defence Production), Ministry of Defence, and Mr. Kim Il Dong, Vice Minister, Defence Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), Republic of Korea.

Mr. Seong Ho Lee, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to India, and Dr. Vijay Namdeorao Zade, Joint Secretary (Naval Systems), Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, also attended the meeting along with senior officials from both countries.

Representatives of leading defence companies from both countries also participated. M/s Larsen & Toubro (L&T) and M/s Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML) participated in the discussions. Republic of Korea was represented by Hanwha Aerospace, Korean Air, Hanwha Systems, Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) and DS Navcours.

On the sidelines of the JCM, Vice Minister, Defence Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), Republic of Korea, Mr. Kim Il Dong, called on Hon’ble Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth. During the interaction, both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral defence cooperation and deepening collaboration in defence industries and logistics.

The 10th JCM reaffirmed the close and growing defence ties between India and the Republic of Korea and provided an important platform for advancing bilateral cooperation in defence production and logistics.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
NATIONAL RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT AGENCY
NRIDA and IIM Kolkata Signed MoU for Four-Year Impact Assessment Study of  PMGSY-IV and PM-JANMAN
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 9:14PM by PIB Delhi

The National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA), Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, and the Indian Institute of Management Kolkata (IIM Kolkata) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for undertaking a comprehensive four-year longitudinal Impact Assessment Study of roads constructed under PMGSY-IV and PM-JANMAN.

The MoU was signed by Ms Aditi Singh (IAS) Director General, NRIDA, on behalf of NRIDA, Ministry of Rural Development Government of India and Prof. Alok Kumar Rai Director, (IIM Kolkata), in the presence of Secretary, Rural Development, Shri Rohit Kansal and other officials of Ministry and IIM Kolkata marking an important step towards strengthening evidence-based impact assessment of rural connectivity interventions.

Key Highlights of the Study

  • Four-year longitudinal impact assessment to assess the long-term outcomes of rural road connectivity.
  • Coverage of 10 States/UTs, 50 districts, 150 blocks and 250 roads. States/UT’s  to be covered are Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Jammu & Kashmir, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Uttarakhand.
  • Survey of approximately 5,000 households to assess changes in mobility, accessibility and socio-economic conditions.
  • The study will follow a longitudinal approach involving Baseline Survey (Pre-Construction Survey) and  Endline Survey (Post Construction Survey) data collection to assess changes over time.
  • Assessment of the impact of rural roads on mobility, accessibility, socio-economic conditions and access to essential services.
  • Baseline Survey (Pre Construction Survey): 14 months
  • Transition Period: Approximately 12 months
  • Endline Survey (Post Construction Survey): 22 months

Expected Outcomes

The long-term study is expected to generate robust evidence on the sustained socio-economic and developmental impacts of rural road connectivity under PMGSY-IV and PM-JANMAN. It will assess how improved connectivity influences accessibility and mobility, livelihoods, employment, income diversification, agriculture, non-farm activities and access to markets as well as household welfare and rural deprivation.

 

The study will also assess the long-term impact of improved rural road connectivity on education, healthcare, women’s empowerment, safety, and access to essential public and financial services. Particular emphasis will be given to changes observed in travel time and transportation costs, mobility, access to employment and livelihood opportunities and migration patterns. It will further examine changes in these outcomes over time and assess variations across different regions and vulnerable groups, thereby, providing a comprehensive understanding of the long-term impact of rural road connectivity.

An important outcome will be the assessment of the sustainability of these benefits in ensuring continued socio-economic gains. The proposed study may help in identifying implementation gaps, emerging challenges and areas requiring policy intervention.

Overall, the collaboration between NRIDA, MoRD and IIM Kolkata will provide valuable inputs for programme review, outcome monitoring, evidence-based policy formulation and future planning in rural infrastructure development.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
UIDAI unveils five new initiatives at Aadhaar Samvaad Kolkata to further advance trusted digital identity and good governance
Hon’ble MoS Sh Jitin Prasada said Aadhaar is a very critical component for India’s growth story and emphasized the role of Aadhaar in improving ease of living
Over 600 senior policy makers, industry players and innovators came together to deliberate the way forward
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 8:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) today conducted a day long stakeholders conference with ecosystem partners to deliberate and share ideas to further enhance service delivery, improve convenience by using Aadhaar and contribute to the larger good of people.

Over 600 stakeholders including senior policy makers, industry leaders, technocrats, and professionals came together for the ‘Aadhaar Samvaad’ in Kolkata, which coincided with the 17th Aadhaar Day. 

The event was graced by Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State, Ministry of Commerce and Industry and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology as the chief guest and marked an important milestone in Aadhaar's continuing evolution as a trusted digital identity infrastructure for India.

“Aadhaar is a great success story. Aadhaar is a very critical component for India’s growth story,” Prasada said.

“Aadhaar has been instrumental in enhancing service delivery, promoting mass scale financial inclusion, and ensuring that government benefits, reach the right people. As a cornerstone of our digital governance, Aadhaar has revolutionized the way we access government services, ensuring transparency, efficiency, and inclusivity,” Prasada added, and underlined the importance of staying in sync with the emerging technologies.

He also underlined how Aadhaar is going to be beneficial for the people of West Bengal and benefits will reach the right beneficiaries of government initiatives.

CEO UIDAI Sh Saurabh Vijay said resident continues to remain at the centre of every action of UIDAI and Aadhaar ecosystem. He underlined that the product launches on the 17th Aadhaar Day is in sync with this resident centricity philosophy.

“Throughout the day, we discussed with our stakeholders on issues like expanding usage of Aadhaar, further strengthening authentication ecosystem for good governance, the enrolment and update ecosystem, and challenges and opportunities of emerging technologies,” Vijay said.

“Today is also an occasion to recognise that Aadhaar continues to evolve with the changing needs of a rapidly transforming digital India. New technologies, new forms of service delivery and stronger emphasis on privacy, security and resident convenience are shaping its next chapter,” said Vivek C Verma, Deputy Director General, UIDAI in his welcome address.

The occasion witnessed the launch of five new initiatives aimed at enhancing resident convenience, strengthening security, enabling good governance and preparing the Aadhaar ecosystem for the next phase of digital transformation.

A key launch was Face Authentication for the Electronic Public Distribution System (ePDS), jointly undertaken by UIDAI, the Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD) and the National Informatics Centre (NIC). The consent-based, contactless authentication option provides beneficiaries with an additional mode of authentication, particularly in situations where fingerprint authentication may be difficult, and enables States and Union Territories to integrate Face Authentication into their ePDS ecosystems.

UIDAI also launched SWIK Portal 2.0, which streamlines the process for seeking approval for Aadhaar authentication under the Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance framework. Eligible non-Government entities can now submit proposals for permissible use cases directly through the portal to the concerned Ministry/Department, enabling a structured and coordinated approval process. https://swik.meity.gov.in/

The Sub-AUA/Sub-KUA (LITE) Framework launched today will facilitate wider adoption of Aadhaar authentication by Government and eligible other than Government entities with low-volume requirements. Eligible entities can leverage the authentication infrastructure of an existing AUA/KUA, enabling simpler and faster onboarding in real time without establishing any authentication infrastructure, while adhering to UIDAI’s security, privacy and regulatory requirements.

UIDAI also unveiled a new Token Management System, which will make it easier for people to go to state and regional offices of UIDAI for services wherever applicable.

Revamped UIDAI website:

Prasad unveiled a revamped UIDAI website, which will make information flow real time on its website. Residents come to UIDAI for four fundamental reasons: understand Aadhaar, access a service, find a document, or seek assistance. The redesigned website brings these journeys into a clearer structure.

The website has been designed in alignment with the Aadhaar brand guidelines, establishing a consistent visual identity across the UIDAI website, the myAadhaar portal and the Aadhaar App.

Accessibility has been a key consideration in the design of the revamped website. It incorporates features such as screen-reader compatibility, adjustable font sizes, improved colour contrast, keyboard navigation, and other accessibility enhancements to make Aadhaar-related information and services more accessible and inclusive for all residents, including persons with disabilities.

With BHASHINI integration, the website supports 13 languages, including English and Hindi. We are planning to make the website available in 23 languages in near future – up from 13 today.

The revamped website also introduces the UIDAI Career Portal, enabling online applications for deputation opportunities and providing a more streamlined and transparent process for prospective applicants.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
District Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes Held at Okhla Industrial Estate, New Delhi as part of Shram Samvad Initiative
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 8:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour & Employment, in collaboration with FICCI and Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co., organised a "Shram Samvad" - District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on Labour Codes at Okhla Industrial Estate, New Delhi. The programme aimed to build awareness among employers and industry stakeholders on the Labour Codes, which came into force on 21st November 2025, and the Central Rules notified on 8 May 2026, while highlighting the key provisions and compliance requirements under the new framework. The programme brought together more than 100 participants from diverse sectors, including employers, industry representatives, HR professionals, legal experts, finance specialists, and other key stakeholders in the labour and employment ecosystem.

The programme featured a series of technical sessions designed to provide participants with practical insights into the Labour Codes, employer obligations, and key social security initiatives of the Government of India.

The inaugural session was addressed by Dr P K Jena, Director, Ministry of Labour and Employment, along with Ms Pallavi Shroff, Executive Committee Member and Managing Partner, Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co. Ms Pooja Ramchandani, Partner, Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co moderated the session.

The first technical session was delivered by Dr P.K. Jena who presented a comprehensive overview of the Labour Codes, their objectives, and the major reforms introduced through the new legislative framework. The session helped participants understand the broader vision and significance of labour law reforms for both employers and workers.

The second session was conducted by Mohd. Nadeem, Labour Enforcement Officer, PMU, Ministry of Labour & Employment, focusing on the key compliance requirements for employers under the Labour Codes. The session provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, enabling participants to better understand the operational aspects of the new framework.

The third session focused on the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and was led by Shri Manish Kumar Singh, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I, Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). Participants were briefed on the scheme's objectives, eligibility conditions, and benefits aimed at promoting employment generation.

The fourth session covered the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Scheme and was conducted by Shri Sandeep Chourasia, Welfare Administrator, DGLW, Ministry of Labour & Employment. The session highlighted the scheme's key features and its role in extending pension and social security benefits to workers in the unorganised sector.

The programme concluded with an interactive Question and Answer session, during which participants engaged directly with the speakers and sought clarifications on various aspects of the Labour Codes, employer compliances, and social security schemes.

The event served as an important platform for capacity building, stakeholder engagement, and awareness generation, fostering a deeper understanding of the Labour Codes and supporting their effective implementation through informed participation by employers and industry stakeholders.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
“By treating the landscape, twin objectives of watershed development as well as river rejuvenation can be achieved”- Secretary, DoLR, Shri Narendra Bhooshan
Posted On: 29 SEP 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi

Department of Land Resources organised a National Workshop on proposed Pilot projects on River Rejuvenation through the watershed approach, at New Delhi on 29 September 2026.

Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Shri Narendra Bhooshan, emphasised that river rejuvenation requires treating the landscapes that feed rivers, with interventions tailored to the specific hydrological conditions of each catchment.

The Workshop brought together hydrologists, groundwater experts, geospatial scientists from IITs, experts from ICAR Institutes, National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Central Ground Water Board, NMCG, National River Conservation Directorate (NRCD), Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, National Institute of Hydrology (NIH), National Geophysical Research Institute, Watershed practitioners, State Government representatives, research institutions, NGOs and International Organisations to deliberate on a scientific framework for river rejuvenation through watershed development.

Secretary, DoLR, Shri Narendra Bhooshan, stated that the proposed pilots will focus on restoring river hydrology through catchment treatment, groundwater recharge, soil and water conservation, and improvement of base and lean-season flows.

He emphasised that “River/Streams Rejuvenation through Watershed Development Approach” can achieve twin objectives of watershed development as well as river rejuvenation. We need to scientifically understand the hydrology of each catchment and establish whether targeted interventions can restore the lost hydrological function of a river or stream.”

He emphasised that planning should be based on a hydrological baseline, including rainfall, groundwater, catchment condition and water balance.

CEO, National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), Dr. Chandra Shekhar Kumar, as Chief Guest of the programme, said, “For small rivers, where long-term flow data is often limited, we need a systematic data-based framework that brings together legacy data, scientific analysis, high-resolution mapping and Decision Support Systems to guide river selection and treatment planning.”

Joint Secretary, Watershed Management, DoLR, Shri Nitin Khade, said, “The objective of these pilots is to increase river flows through groundwater recharge, soil and water conservation and intensive watershed treatment, while simultaneously improving agricultural productivity and income of farmers residing in the catchment areas. The challenge is to achieve both objectives in a balanced manner.”

Shri Khade said that the proposed pilots will focus on first-, second-, and third-order streams, with selection based on parameters including historical decline in flow, catchment condition, rainfall, groundwater depletion, intervention potential and data availability.

The workshop also highlighted the importance of convergence with government programmes and schemes, including VB-G RAM G, CAMPA, Ministry of Jal Shakti and State schemes and programmes, CSR, NGOs, along with support from research institutions and international organisations. The workshop emphasized on giving effect to Whole of Government and Whole of Society Approach.

The workshop deliberated on river selection, hydrological baselines, catchment treatment, GIS and remote sensing, intervention design, institutional frameworks, multidisciplinary teams, monitoring and evaluation, convergence, community participation and long-term maintenance.

The proposed monitoring framework will assess outcomes across four dimensions: Hydrological, Environmental, Agricultural and Socio-economic, with the objective of generating evidence that can guide the potential scaling up of watershed development approach based river rejuvenation across the country.
